summary.en: Designed toward future CME accreditation, this post-graduate clinical course prepares aesthetic and dermatologic clinicians to appraise the endocrine physiology of skin, differentiate pathognomonic endocrine cutaneous signs from isolated cosmetic presentations, evaluate the GRADE evidence and pharmacodynamics of cutaneous peptides and incretin therapies, and navigate regulatory and liability boundaries without promoting unapproved dosing protocols or commercial bias.

client.productContext: A peptides-for-skin course for clinicians from Hormonaly Academy, built on Perceptors.

personas: dermatologist, aesthetic physician or plastic surgeon evaluating hormone and peptide claims for skin
nurse practitioner or physician associate who prescribes or counsels in aesthetic, dermatology or primary care
registered nurse, aesthetic nurse or injector who delivers treatments and fields patient questions
other licensed providers (pharmacists, naturopathic doctors, allied aesthetic professionals) who advise on skin products and referrals

professionalScope.en: Continuing professional education for licensed clinicians and allied providers. Every learner gets the same evidence, regulatory status and safety content; what each may do with it — prescribe, recommend, administer, or refer — follows their own licence and scope, and the course adapts its practice guidance to that role. It informs clinical reasoning; it is not a protocol, contains no dosing, and does not replace specialist input, formal guidelines or individual judgment.

disclaimers.en: Educational content for clinicians. It does not prescribe, and it never restates an evidence grade above what the source assigns to the specific indication.

Regulatory statements name their jurisdiction and date. US status (FDA, 503A/503B compounding) is given in the lesson text; status in the United Kingdom, the European Union, Portugal, Brazil and the United Arab Emirates (federal, with Dubai and Abu Dhabi where they differ) is given in each moment's regulatory note, read from each regulator's own primary sources in September 2026, and the learner's own country is shown first. The US compounding categories have no equivalent in the other jurisdictions. Check the live status with the national regulator before acting.
Designed toward future CME accreditation. No CME or CE credit is currently offered.

layers.detail: Product status mapped for the UK: MHRA-licensed products checked in UK product information (semaglutide as Ozempic and Wegovy, tirzepatide as Mounjaro, baricitinib, minoxidil, finasteride, somatropin, estradiol HRT, topical tretinoin), afamelanotide's UK licence (via NICE HST27), no UK product information for tesamorelin, sermorelin or ipamorelin (MHRA products database), somatropin as a Class C controlled drug, and the cosmetic (assimilated Regulation 1223/2009) and food-supplement (Food Supplements (England) Regulations 2003) categories. Modules 02–06. UK statements added 2026-09-25; confirmed by Fady Hannah-Shmouni, MD FRCPC on 2026-09-25.

Claims and advertising mapped for the UK: no sale, supply or advertising of a medicine without a UK marketing authorisation (Human Medicines Regulations 2012, regs 46 and 279), no advertising of prescription-only medicines to the public (reg. 284; CAP Code 12.12; MHRA Blue Guide; ASA ruling of 11 Feb 2026), cosmetic claims (Regulation 1223/2009 art. 20; ASA ruling of 13 May 2026 on a peptide serum), and food disease and health claims (Regulation 1169/2011 art. 7(3); Regulation 1924/2006 art. 10). Modules 04 and 07. UK statements added 2026-09-25; confirmed by Fady Hannah-Shmouni, MD FRCPC on 2026-09-25.

Practice mapped for the UK: the 'specials' route (reg. 167) and pharmacy preparation (Medicines Act 1968 s. 10) in place of 503A/503B, MHRA Guidance Note 14's order of preference (licensed, off-label, imported, special), prescriber responsibility (GMC paras 102–108, MHRA Drug Safety Update 2009, GPhC 2025, NMC Code 18), GMC's physical examination before injectable cosmetic medicines, MHRA's finasteride warnings (May 2026) and enforcement (retatrutide; the May 2026 seizure including peptide products; melanotan). Two new moments in module 07 (m7-p21, m7-p22); role versions changed only where the practice line differs by jurisdiction. UK statements added 2026-09-25; confirmed by Fady Hannah-Shmouni, MD FRCPC on 2026-09-25.

Every row returned was 'Active'; the directory has no status filter, so withdrawn or cancelled registrations may not appear. Rows give classification, strength, form, manufacturer, status and registration date; detail pages add dispensing mode and a therapeutic category but no indications. Quotes join table cells with ' | ' and page fields with spaces; '…' marks omitted cells or fields. 'BPC' as an ingredient matched only two unrelated products whose ingredients carry the 'BPC' pharmacopoeia suffix (Permethrin BPC, Cajuput Oil BPC). citations.title: Neuro-immuno-endocrinology of the skin: how environment regulates body homeostasis
citations.authors: Slominski RM, Raman C, Jetten AM, Slominski AT

note.en: narrative review · academic · role: A&RE ch.6 ref 1 — the four immuno-endocrine units (epidermal, dermal, hypodermal, adnexal) and the three routes (local, neural, circulation) · PMID 40263492 · Publisher correction PMID 40316721. Guide reference resolves exactly.

citations.title: Neuroendocrinology of the skin

note.en: narrative review · academic · role: A&RE ch.5 ref 3, ch.6 ref 3, ch.7 ref 4 — CRH, POMC, ACTH, α-MSH and β-endorphin are made in skin with their receptors (para/autocrine action); dermal and epidermal units · PMID 11041445 · Erratum 2002. Also cited by A&RE ch.7 for the estrogen–senescence statement, which this 2000 review does not address (see findings).

citations.title: The human skin as a hormone target and an endocrine gland

note.en: narrative review · academic · role: A&RE ch.5 ref 4, ch.7 ref 2 — skin makes, activates and releases hormones, including sex steroids that matter for the whole organism, especially in older people · PMID 16982574 · Verified; no PMCID.

citations.title: Neuronal control of skin function: the skin as a neuroimmunoendocrine organ
citations.authors: Roosterman D, Goerge T, Schneider SW, Bunnett NW, Steinhoff M

note.en: narrative review · academic · role: A&RE ch.5 ref 13 — sensory nerves and neuropeptides as the neural arm of the skin's signalling network · PMID 17015491 · Verified.

citations.title: Steroidogenesis in the skin: implications for local immune functions
citations.authors: Slominski A, Zbytek B, Nikolakis G, et al.

note.en: narrative review · academic · role: A&RE ch.6 ref 4 — skin cells hold the full apparatus (CYP11A1 onward) to make glucocorticoids, androgens and estrogens or activate circulating precursors; the review also describes a skin contribution to circulating androgens and estrogens · PMID 23435015 · Verified.

citations.title: Keratinocytes control skin immune homeostasis through de novo-synthesized glucocorticoids
citations.authors: Phan TS, Schink L, Mann J, et al.

note.en: mouse genetic model (keratinocyte Cyp11b1 deletion) plus human disease association · academic · role: A&RE ch.6 ref 5 — keratinocyte-made glucocorticoids restrain skin inflammation; the functional proof is in mice · PMID 33514551 · The guide presents this without naming the species; the course labels it as animal evidence.

citations.title: Human hair follicles display a functional equivalent of the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis and synthesize cortisol
citations.authors: Ito N, Ito T, Kromminga A, et al.

note.en: human scalp hair follicles in organ culture (ex vivo) · academic · role: A&RE ch.6 ref 11 — CRH → POMC/ACTH → cortisol secretion with glucocorticoid feedback on CRH, in follicles with no systemic connections · PMID 15946990 · Verified.

citations.title: Human Hair Follicles Operate a Functional Peripheral Equivalent of the Hypothalamic-Pituitary-Somatotropic Axis Ex Vivo
citations.authors: Horesh EJ, Gherardini J, Alam M, et al.

note.en: research letter; human follicles ex vivo · academic · role: A&RE ch.6 ref 12 — a GH/IGF-1 loop in the follicle · PMID 36496194 · No abstract indexed and not open access; cited only for the finding its title states.

citations.title: Thyroid hormone action in epidermal development and homeostasis and its implications in the pathophysiology of the skin
citations.authors: Mancino G, Miro C, Di Cicco E, Dentice M

note.en: narrative review (mouse models of thyroid-hormone metabolism) · academic · role: A&RE ch.6 ref 7 — local deiodinase control of T3 in keratinocytes; the review says the mechanisms are being clarified mainly in mouse models · PMID 33683663 · Verified.

citations.title: Photosynthesis of previtamin D3 in human skin and the physiologic consequences
citations.authors: Holick MF, MacLaughlin JA, Clark MB, et al.

note.en: human skin photobiology · academic · role: the skin-to-body example: previtamin D3 forms in human skin under solar UV and vitamin D3 is carried into the circulation by vitamin D-binding protein · PMID 6251551 · Not cited by either guide; added as the primary for the statement that skin supplies a whole-body hormone system.

citations.title: Vitamin D metabolism, mechanism of action, and clinical applications

note.en: narrative review · academic · role: A&RE ch.7 ref 3 — vitamin D3 made in skin from 7-dehydrocholesterol, then 25(OH)D and 1,25(OH)2D elsewhere · PMID 24529992 · Verified.

citations.title: Thyroid hormone action on skin

note.en: clinical review · academic · role: A&RE ch.5 ref 8 — the skin signs of thyroid disease (myxoedema; dry, coarse skin) · PMID 22110782 · Verified (a 2012 review with the same title exists, PMID 22914563; the guide's volume and pages match this one).

citations.title: A Hormone Cell Atlas maps the human endocrine system at cellular resolution
citations.authors: Fei L, Huang-Doran I, Lawler K, et al. (senior authors Teichmann SA, Farooqi IS)

note.en: single-cell and single-nucleus transcriptomic atlas (hormone2cell): 379 hormone and receptor genes, ~14 million cells and nuclei, 47 human tissues · academic (University of Cambridge, Wellcome Sanger Institute) · role: A&RE ch.7 ref 1 — predicted hormone-producing and hormone-receiving cell types; the transcriptomic map the lesson is about · PMID 42207862 · PubMed entry 2026-05-28 (the guide's 'published online May 28, 2026'); print issue 2 Jul 2026. Full text and supplement paywalled (HTTP 403); only abstract- and portal-level facts are taught.

citations.title: Hormone Cell Atlas portal — About and FAQs
citations.authors: Hormone Cell Atlas team (Farooqi and Teichmann groups)

note.en: data portal · atlas authors · role: the authors' own usage statement: predictions are 'putative and hypothesis-generating, rather than … functional hormones and receptors', validation is the user's responsibility; 47 disease-free tissues, 1,900+ cell types, 14 million+ cells; skin is listed among the tissues on the sister cellxgene site (hormonecellatlas.cellgeni.sanger.ac.uk) · Fetched live 2026-09-24 (HTTP 200).

citations.title: On the Dependency of Cellular Protein Levels on mRNA Abundance
citations.authors: Liu Y, Beyer A, Aebersold R

note.en: narrative review · academic · role: transcript levels by themselves are not sufficient to predict protein levels in many scenarios · PMID 27104977 · Not cited by either guide; added to support the RNA-versus-protein step.

citations.title: The effect of sunscreen on vitamin D: a review
citations.authors: Neale RE, Khan SR, Lucas RM, Waterhouse M, Whiteman DC, Olsen CM

note.en: systematic review (MOOSE): 4 experimental studies, 3 field trials (2 RCTs), 69 observational studies · academic (QIMR Berghofer, Australian National University) · role: tests the guide's pearl that serum 25(OH)D falls with sunscreen use: experiments with artificial UV show a block; randomized field trials of daily sunscreen (SPF ~16) show no fall; high-SPF products untested · PMID 30945275 · Not cited by either guide; contradicts A&RE ch.7 testing pearl (see findings).

citations.title: Senescence-associated secretory phenotypes reveal cell-nonautonomous functions of oncogenic RAS and the p53 tumor suppressor
citations.authors: Coppé JP, Patil CK, Rodier F, et al.

note.en: cultured human fibroblasts and epithelial cells after genotoxic stress (+ prostate tumours after chemotherapy) · academic · role: defines the SASP (IL-6, IL-8 and other secreted factors) — the concept the guide uses · PMID 19053174 · Not cited by either guide; the primary behind 'SASP'.

citations.title: p16INK4A is a robust in vivo biomarker of cellular aging in human skin
citations.authors: Ressler S, Bartkova J, Niederegger H, et al.

note.en: human skin tissue bank, cross-sectional (0–20, 21–70, 71–95 years) · academic · role: p16-positive cells are more numerous in older skin, in both epidermis and dermis · PMID 16911562 · Not cited by either guide.

citations.title: P16INK4a Positive Cells in Human Skin Are Indicative of Local Elastic Fiber Morphology, Facial Wrinkling, and Perceived Age
citations.authors: Waaijer ME, Gunn DA, Adams PD, et al.
citations.publication: J Gerontol A Biol Sci Med Sci · 2016;71:1022–1028

note.en: cohort (Leiden Longevity Study), n=178, aged 45–81, sun-protected upper-inner-arm biopsies · academic; one co-author from Unilever; NIH and Cancer Research UK grants · role: senescent-cell counts in human skin track with elastic-fibre changes, facial wrinkles and perceived age, independent of chronological age; lowest vs highest tertile of epidermal p16 counts looked ~3 years younger · PMID 26286607 · Not cited by either guide.

citations.title: Faces of cellular senescence in skin aging

note.en: narrative review · academic · role: A&RE ch.7 ref 5 — senescent cells accumulate in several human skin compartments; cell types respond differently · PMID 34166688 · Verified.

citations.title: Biomarkers of Cellular Senescence and Skin Aging

note.en: narrative review · academic · role: A&RE ch.7 ref 6 — no universal biomarker identifies senescent cells unequivocally; markers by skin compartment · PMID 30190724 · Full text (PMC6115505) read: it does not discuss estrogen loss or hormone responsiveness, which A&RE ch.7 cites it for.

citations.title: Targeting cellular senescence in dermatology: senolytic and senomorphic strategies
citations.authors: Haykal D, Flament F, Garibyan L, Lee K, Escot J, Gueniche A, Kirkland J

note.en: narrative review (no new data) · three authors from L'Oréal and a senolytic-field investigator; declares no competing interests · role: how dermatologic senotherapy stands in 2026: a review of mechanism and prospects; transient senescence aids wound repair · PMID 42417965 · Not cited by either guide.

citations.title: The influence of age and sex on skin thickness, skin collagen and density
citations.authors: Shuster S, Black MM, McVitie E

note.en: cross-sectional reference measurements of forearm skin · academic · role: A&RE ch.5 ref 1 — skin collagen falls with age and is lower in women at all ages · PMID 1220811 · The abstract gives no annual rate; the guide's '~1% per year' could not be checked and is not taught.

citations.title: Decreased collagen production in chronologically aged skin: roles of age-dependent alteration in fibroblast function and defective mechanical stimulation
citations.authors: Varani J, Dame MK, Rittie L, et al.

note.en: human skin sections (18–29 vs 80+ years) and isolated dermal fibroblasts · academic · role: aged fibroblasts make less procollagen and are less attached to and stretched by collagen — two routes to lower synthesis · PMID 16723701 · Not cited by either guide.

citations.title: Collagen fragmentation promotes oxidative stress and elevates matrix metalloproteinase-1 in fibroblasts in aged human skin
citations.authors: Fisher GJ, Quan T, Purohit T, et al.

note.en: aged (>80) vs young (21–30) human skin in vivo, plus organ and collagen-lattice culture · academic · role: more fibroblast MMP-1 in aged human dermis; fragmented collagen lowers fibroblast stretch and raises MMP-1 and oxidants — a self-perpetuating loop · PMID 19116368 · Not cited by either guide.

citations.title: Mechanisms of photoaging and chronological skin aging
citations.authors: Fisher GJ, Kang S, Varani J, et al.

note.en: narrative review with new data · academic · role: A&RE ch.5 ref 2 — UV drives the matrix breakdown of photoageing, and photoageing and chronological ageing share molecular pathways · PMID 12437452 · Verified.

citations.title: Naturally occurring p16(Ink4a)-positive cells shorten healthy lifespan
citations.authors: Baker DJ, Childs BG, Durik M, et al.

note.en: mouse (INK-ATTAC transgene) · academic · role: A&RE ch.13 ref 2 — clearing p16-positive cells from one year of age extended median lifespan and delayed kidney, heart and fat deterioration; skin was checked for safety only (thickness, fibrosis), and clearance during healing slowed wound closure (Extended Data Fig. 10) · PMID 26840489 · Verified.

citations.title: Senolytics improve physical function and increase lifespan in old age
citations.authors: Xu M, Pirtskhalava T, Farr JN, et al.

note.en: mouse, plus human adipose-tissue explants · several authors hold a financial interest; Mayo Clinic holds senolytic patents · role: A&RE ch.17 ref 1 — senescent cells cause dysfunction when transplanted; senolytics improved function and post-treatment survival in old mice · PMID 29988130 · Verified.

citations.title: Senolytics decrease senescent cells in humans: Preliminary report from a clinical trial of Dasatinib plus Quercetin in individuals with diabetic kidney disease
citations.authors: Hickson LJ, Langhi Prata LGP, Bobart SA, et al.

note.en: open-label phase 1 pilot, n=9, diabetic kidney disease (NCT02848131) · investigators with a financial interest; Mayo Clinic holds patents · role: A&RE ch.17 ref 3 — after a short course, epidermal p16- and p21-positive cells and circulating SASP factors fell; tissue-marker endpoints only · PMID 31542391 · Corrigendum PMID 31982828. The course does not report doses.

citations.title: Topical rapamycin reduces markers of senescence and aging in human skin: an exploratory, prospective, randomized trial
citations.authors: Chung CL, Lawrence I, Hoffman M, et al.

note.en: exploratory placebo-controlled RCT; 36 enrolled, 19 discontinued or lost to follow-up (NCT03103893) · academic (Drexel University) · role: the one randomized study of a senomorphic in human skin found: p16 protein fell and collagen VII rose; clinical change described only in 'multiple participants' · PMID 31761958 · Not cited by either guide.

citations.title: Sunscreen and prevention of skin aging: a randomized trial
citations.authors: Hughes MC, Williams GM, Baker P, Green AC

note.en: community RCT (Nambour), n=903 adults under 55, 4.5 years, blinded assessors (ACTRN12610000086066) · public (National Health and Medical Research Council of Australia) · role: daily sunscreen: no detectable increase in skin ageing over 4.5 years and 24% less ageing than discretionary use · PMID 23732711 · Not cited by either guide (A&RE ch.10 recommends sun protection without a trial citation).

citations.title: Topical tretinoin for treating photoaging: A systematic review of randomized controlled trials
citations.authors: Sitohang IBS, Makes WI, Sandora N, Suryanegara J

note.en: systematic review of 7 RCTs · academic; no conflicts declared · role: the randomized-trial base behind the guide's GRADE A for topical retinoids in photoageing: consistent improvement in wrinkling, mottled pigmentation and lentigines · PMID 35620028 · A&RE gives no citation for its GRADE A; this review supplies one.

citations.title: Improvement of naturally aged skin with vitamin A (retinol)
citations.authors: Kafi R, Kwak HS, Schumacher WE, et al.

note.en: randomized double-blind vehicle-controlled arm comparison, n=36, mean age 87, 24 weeks · academic (NIH-supported) · role: retinol improved fine wrinkling of naturally aged skin; biopsy subgroups showed more glycosaminoglycan and procollagen I · PMID 17515510 · Not cited by either guide. Concentrations are not reported by the course.

citations.title: Vitamin A antagonizes decreased cell growth and elevated collagen-degrading matrix metalloproteinases and stimulates collagen accumulation in naturally aged human skin
citations.authors: Varani J, Warner RL, Gharaee-Kermani M, et al.

note.en: human sun-protected skin by age group (n=72) plus one-week topical retinol in 53 people aged 80+ · academic · role: aged skin shows more MMPs and less collagen synthesis; one week of topical retinol lowered MMPs and raised collagen synthesis · PMID 10692106 · Not cited by either guide. Concentrations are not reported by the course.

citations.title: Localization, age- and site-dependent expression, and regulation of 11β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 1 in skin
citations.authors: Tiganescu A, Walker EA, Hardy RS, Mayes AE, Stewart PM

note.en: human skin explants and primary dermal fibroblasts; mouse skin · academic (University of Birmingham) · role: keratinocytes and dermal fibroblasts express 11β-HSD1 (not 11β-HSD2); activity rises with donor age; photo-exposed fibroblasts express more; glucocorticoid availability is regulated at a pre-receptor level, independently of systemic levels · PMID 20739946 · A&RE ch.8 ref 2; verified

citations.title: 11β-Hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase blockade prevents age-induced skin structure and function defects
citations.authors: Tiganescu A, Tahrani AA, Morgan SA, et al.

note.en: human skin biopsies (young vs older; photo-exposed vs photo-protected) + 11β-HSD1 knockout mice · academic (University of Birmingham) · role: 11β-HSD1 activity elevated in aged and photo-exposed human skin; knockout mice protected from age-induced dermal atrophy; physiological cortisol inhibits collagen biosynthesis in dermal fibroblasts · PMID 23722901 · not cited by the guides; open access PMC3696573

citations.title: Oral 11β-HSD1 inhibitor AZD4017 improves wound healing and skin integrity in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus: a pilot randomized controlled trial
citations.authors: Ajjan RA, Hensor EMA, Del Galdo F, et al.

note.en: investigator-initiated double-blind placebo-controlled phase 2b pilot, n=28 adults with type 2 diabetes, 35 days · academic lead (University of Leeds); AstraZeneca co-authors · role: the only human RCT of 11β-HSD1 inhibition with skin outcomes: primary outcome (ex vivo skin 11β-HSD1 activity) not met; exploratory smaller wound diameter; improved epidermal integrity but modestly impaired barrier function · PMID 35113805 · not cited by the guides; registered NCT03313297; the drug regimen is deliberately not reproduced (the lock excludes dosing)

citations.title: Glucocorticoids and Skin Healing in Diabetes (GC-SHealD)

note.en: registered phase 2 pilot · academic · role: status: the only registered trial of an 11β-HSD1 inhibitor with skin outcomes found (ClinicalTrials.gov v2 API, 2026-09-24, terms '11beta-HSD1', '11-beta hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 1 inhibitor', AZD4017, SPI-62, clofutriben); none tests skin ageing. AZD4017 has no Drugs@FDA record (openFDA drugsfda query, 2026-09-24) · CT.gov API 2026-09-24; results published as Ajjan 2022

citations.title: The diagnosis of Cushing's syndrome: an Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline
citations.authors: Nieman LK, Biller BMK, Findling JW, et al.

note.en: clinical practice guideline (GRADE) · professional society (Endocrine Society) · role: A&RE ch.8 ref 5. Table 1: features that best discriminate Cushing's syndrome = easy bruising, facial plethora, proximal myopathy, striae (especially reddish-purple and >1 cm wide); common and/or less discriminatory = facial fullness, dorsocervical fat pad, supraclavicular fullness, weight gain, obesity, acne, hirsutism, thin skin, fatigue, insomnia. 3.1 drug history first (oral, rectal, inhaled, topical, injected; skin creams incl. bleaching agents, herbal tonics, joint or nerve injections). 3.2 test multiple and progressive features or features unusual for age. 3.3 against widespread testing. 3.5 against random serum cortisol. Abnormal result → endocrinologist. Endogenous incidence 2–3 per million per year (European population studies); commonest cause iatrogenic. · PMID 18334580 · full text read at pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov (PMC2386281) 2026-09-24; test names only, doses not reproduced

citations.title: Estrogens and aging skin

note.en: narrative review · academic · role: A&RE ch.9 ref 2 and the single reference NAMS 2022 cites for its skin key point; quotes collagen falling 'by as much as 30% in the first five years after menopause' citing Brincat 1985 and Affinito 1999 · PMID 24194966 · open access PMC3772914, read in full 2026-09-24

citations.title: Induction of collagen by estradiol: difference between sun-protected and photodamaged human skin in vivo
citations.authors: Rittié L, Kang S, Voorhees JJ, Fisher GJ

note.en: vehicle-controlled in vivo biopsy study, n=70 (40 postmenopausal women, 30 men, mean age 75), 2 weeks · academic (University of Michigan) · role: ERα, ERβ and GPR30 expressed similarly in aged and photoaged skin; topical estradiol raised procollagen I/III and collagen I in sun-protected hip skin but not in photoaged forearm or face · PMID 18794456 · registered NCT00113100; concentrations deliberately not reproduced

citations.title: Long-term effects of the menopause and sex hormones on skin thickness
citations.authors: Brincat M, Moniz CJ, Studd JW, et al.

note.en: biopsy comparison of implant-treated vs untreated postmenopausal women · academic (London) · role: in untreated women skin collagen declined in relation to years since menopause, not chronological age · PMID 3978054 · cited by Thornton 2013 for the 30% figure; the abstract does not state it

citations.title: A study of the decrease of skin collagen content, skin thickness, and bone mass in the postmenopausal woman
citations.authors: Brincat M, Kabalan S, Studd JW, et al.

note.en: observational study of postmenopausal women · academic (London) · role: skin collagen content, skin thickness and bone mass each declined by 1–2% per year after menopause, related to years since menopause · PMID 3120067 · primary source for the per-year figure

citations.title: Effects of postmenopausal hypoestrogenism on skin collagen
citations.authors: Affinito P, Palomba S, Sorrentino C, et al.

note.en: biopsy study, n=32 (14 pre-, 18 postmenopausal) · academic (Naples) · role: type I and III collagen lower after menopause; inversely correlated with years since menopause (and with age) · PMID 10656502 · cited by Thornton 2013 for the 30% figure; the abstract does not state it

citations.title: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study on the effect of conjugated estrogens on skin thickness
citations.authors: Maheux R, Naud F, Rioux M, et al.

note.en: double-blind placebo-controlled RCT, n=60, 12 months · academic (Québec); sponsor not stated in abstract · role: systemic conjugated estrogens increased skin thickness (biopsy, great-trochanter skin) vs placebo · PMID 8116726 · not cited by the guides; cited by Thornton 2013

citations.title: The effects of systemic hormonal replacement therapy on the skin of postmenopausal women
citations.authors: Sauerbronn AV, Fonseca AM, Bagnoli VR, et al.

note.en: double-blind placebo-controlled RCT, n=41, 6 months · academic (São Paulo) · role: upper-arm skin collagen rose 6.49% with HT only; other skin parameters unchanged · PMID 10687834 · not cited by the guides; regimen deliberately not reproduced

citations.title: Does hormone therapy improve age-related skin changes in postmenopausal women? note.en: professional standard · statutory professional regulator · role: UK doctors offering cosmetic interventions must carry out a physical examination before prescribing injectable cosmetic medicines and must not prescribe them by telephone, video link, online or at the request of others for patients they have not examined (11); interventions must rest on the best available evidence about effectiveness, side effects and risks (12) · Read in a browser 2026-09-25; gmc-uk.org answers scripts with HTTP 403, so the automated source check cannot read it.

claims.text: In the UAE, the Emirates Drug Establishment (EDE; 'UAE Drug Corporation' in the official English translation) has been the federal authority regulating medical products since Federal Decree-Law 28/2023 (issued 25 Sep 2023, in force 30 Sep 2023), with the power to approve and register medical products.

claims.text: In the UAE, since 2 January 2025 (Federal Decree-Law 38/2024, which replaced Federal Law 8/2019), no medical product may be imported, distributed, possessed, sold, displayed, used or manufactured for circulation without an EDE marketing approval.
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "Without prejudice to the applicable legislation concerning veterinary preparations, it is not permitted to import, distribute, possess, sell, display, re-market, use, or manufacture any Medical Product in the State for circulation therein, except after obtaining Marketing Approval of any type from the EDE." · grader: research agents under the jurisdiction research brief; statements are regulatory facts, graded context

claims.text: In the UAE, physicians may prescribe a medicine for uses not in its leaflet, or a medicine never submitted for marketing approval, only when necessary, when no equivalent alternative is available and with the patient's approval; compassionate use is excluded from this rule (Federal Decree-Law 38/2024, Art. 42(1)).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "Physicians may not prescribe a Medical Product for new uses not specified in the internal leaflet or electronic leaflet, or prescribe a Medical Product that has not been submitted for Marketing Approval, except when necessary, provided that there is no equivalent alternative available and with the patient approval. The compassionate use of the Medical Product is excluded from the provisions of this Clause." · grader: research agents under the jurisdiction research brief; statements are regulatory facts, graded context

claims.text: In Dubai, the DHA prohibits circulating, prescribing, dispensing, administering or using any peptide product unless it is registered or licensed with the EDE and used within the scope of its licence, and requires registered peptide products to be used strictly within their approved indications (External Circular 0867, 29 July 2026).

claims.text: In the UAE, medical products compounded in licensed compounding pharmacies are exempt from the marketing-approval requirement (Federal Decree-Law 38/2024, Art. 5(2), in force 2 Jan 2025).

claims.text: In the UAE, a compounding pharmacy may not compound essential copies of products holding an EDE marketing approval unless no commercially available product can deliver the expected benefit to the patient, and may not formulate products intended for research, development or experimentation (Federal Decree-Law 38/2024, Art. 95).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "The Compound Pharmacy is prohibited from the following: … 4. Commencing the installation of Medical Products that are essentially copies of Medical Products that have a valid Marketing Approval from the EDE, unless there is no commercially available Medical Product that can achieve the expected direct benefit to the patient health, and similar results could not be obtained by other means. 5. Compounding Pharmacies may not conduct any activities related to improvised, unstudied formulations or the extraction process of medicines and preparations derived from natural sources, and it is not permitted to formulate a Medical Product prepared for research, development or experimentation." · grader: research agents under the jurisdiction research brief; statements are regulatory facts, graded context

claims.text: In Brazil, Olumiant (baricitinib, Eli Lilly) has been registered by ANVISA since 26 Nov 2018; its current label includes severe alopecia areata in adults and adolescents aged 12 or over weighing at least 30 kg, besides rheumatoid arthritis, atopic dermatitis and COVID-19.
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "OLUMIANT é indicado para o tratamento de pacientes adultos e adolescentes, com idade igual ou superior a 12 anos e com peso ≥ 30 kg com alopecia areata grave." (English: "OLUMIANT is indicated for the treatment of adult and adolescent patients aged 12 years or older and weighing ≥ 30 kg with severe alopecia areata.") · grader: research agents under the jurisdiction research brief; statements are regulatory facts, graded context

claims.text: In Brazil, minoxidil is registered as an anti-alopecia medicine (for example Aloxidil 5%, indicated for androgenetic alopecia in adult men); every active minoxidil registration sits in the anti-alopecia class, and the oral antihypertensive Loniten registrations are all inactive (register, 25 Sep 2026).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "Aloxidil® 5% (minoxidil) é indicado no tratamento da alopecia androgênica (calvície hereditária) em homens adultos." (English: "Aloxidil® 5% (minoxidil) is indicated for the treatment of androgenetic alopecia (hereditary baldness) in adult men.") · grader: research agents under the jurisdiction research brief; statements are regulatory facts, graded context

claims.text: In Brazil, 1 mg finasteride products such as Pro Hair are registered for male-pattern hair loss in men and are not indicated for women or children; the Propecia brand registration is inactive (register, 25 Sep 2026).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "PRO HAIR é indicado para o tratamento de homens com calvície de padrão masculino (alopecia androgênica), para aumentar o crescimento e prevenir a queda adicional de cabelo." (English: "PRO HAIR is indicated for the treatment of men with male-pattern baldness (androgenetic alopecia), to increase growth and prevent further hair loss.") · grader: research agents under the jurisdiction research brief; statements are regulatory facts, graded context

claims.text: In Brazil, somatropin is registered (for example Genotropin, Pfizer, registered 12 Aug 2019) for growth disorders in children and for replacement therapy in adults with severe growth hormone deficiency; skin or anti-ageing uses are not labelled indications.

claims.text: In Brazil, topical tretinoin (for example Vitacid, Theraskin) is registered, and its label names cutaneous photoageing as well as acne vulgaris, for dermatological use in adults and patients over 12.
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "Vitacid® é indicado para o tratamento fotoenvelhecimento cutâneo, proporcionando a melhora de alguns sinais associados a essa condição. É indicado também no tratamento da acne vulgar, em que predominam comedões, pápulas e pústulas." (English: "Vitacid® is indicated for the treatment of cutaneous photoageing, improving some signs associated with this condition. It is also indicated for the treatment of acne vulgaris in which comedones, papules and pustules predominate.") · grader: research agents under the jurisdiction research brief; statements are regulatory facts, graded context

claims.text: In Brazil, estradiol for menopausal hormone therapy is registered (for example Oestrogel, Besins); the label read covers menopausal symptoms and prevention of postmenopausal osteoporosis, and skin ageing is not a labelled indication.
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "Oestrogel® é indicado para o tratamento de sinais e sintomas oriundos da deficiência estrogênica relacionados à menopausa natural ou cirúrgica (fogachos, atrofia urogenital, distúrbio no sono e astenia) e prevenção da osteoporose (perda óssea) pós-menopausa." (English: "Oestrogel® is indicated for the treatment of signs and symptoms of oestrogen deficiency related to natural or surgical menopause (hot flushes, urogenital atrophy, sleep disturbance and asthenia) and for prevention of postmenopausal osteoporosis (bone loss).") · grader: research agents under the jurisdiction research brief; statements are regulatory facts, graded context

claims.text: In Brazil, oral collagen is regulated as a food supplement, not a medicine; ANVISA's Jan 2025 guidance lists an approved skin-health claim for 2 kDa bioactive collagen peptides, restricted to products meeting an ANVISA-set minimum content, for adults only.
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "“Os peptídeos bioativos de colágeno hidrolisado com peso molecular médio de 2 kDa auxiliam na manutenção da saúde da pele.”" (English: "“Bioactive hydrolysed collagen peptides with an average molecular weight of 2 kDa help maintain skin health.”") · grader: research agents under the jurisdiction research brief; statements are regulatory facts, graded context

claims.text: In Brazil, a compounded (magistral) preparation must be made individually by the pharmacy against a prescription from an authorised professional that sets its composition, form and dosing (RDC 96/2008 definition).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "PREPARAÇÃO MAGISTRAL - É aquela preparada na farmácia, de forma individualizada, para ser dispensada atendendo a uma prescrição de um profissional habilitado, respeitada a legislação vigente, que estabelece sua composição, forma farmacêutica, posologia e modo de usar." (English: "MAGISTRAL PREPARATION – One prepared in the pharmacy, individually, to be dispensed against a prescription from an authorised professional, in accordance with current legislation, which sets its composition, dosage form, dosing and directions for use.") · grader: research agents under the jurisdiction research brief; statements are regulatory facts, graded context

claims.text: In Brazil, ANVISA stated on 2 Jul 2026 that any substance must have undergone efficacy and safety assessment before it can be compounded, and that compounding may only be individual, on a medical prescription, by a compounding pharmacy licensed by local health surveillance.
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "Para ser manipulada, qualquer substância precisa ter passado por análises de eficácia e segurança. Além disso, a manipulação de qualquer fórmula SÓ pode ocorrer de forma individualizada, com apresentação de receita médica, por farmácias de manipulação que estejam devidamente regularizadas na vigilância sanitária local." (English: "To be compounded, any substance must have undergone efficacy and safety assessments. In addition, compounding of any formula may ONLY take place individually, on presentation of a medical prescription, by compounding pharmacies duly licensed by local health surveillance.") · grader: research agents under the jurisdiction research brief; statements are regulatory facts, graded context

claims.text: In Brazil, ANVISA stated in Nov 2024 that compounded medicines should be used only when the registered industrial product is unavailable in the dose or dosage form the patient needs, and that only APIs with a current or past registration may be compounded into hormonal implants.
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "A Anvisa ressalta que medicamentos manipulados devem ser utilizados somente diante da indisponibilidade do produto industrializado, registrado na Agência, na dosagem ou forma farmacêutica específica necessária ao paciente, e a partir de avaliação e da prescrição do profissional médico responsável." (English: "Anvisa stresses that compounded medicines should be used only when the industrialised product registered with the Agency is unavailable in the specific dose or dosage form the patient needs, and following assessment and prescription by the responsible physician.") · grader: research agents under the jurisdiction research brief; statements are regulatory facts, graded context

claims.text: In Brazil, Nota Técnica 200/2025 (Aug 2025) allows compounding of GLP-1 agonists only in narrow conditions: synthetic APIs only if a registered medicine with the same molecule exists, biotech APIs only from the manufacturer assessed at registration, with mandatory quality testing; at that date synthetic semaglutide could not be imported or compounded.
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "No caso dos IFAs obtidos por síntese química, a manipulação é permitida desde que já existam medicamentos registrados no Brasil com a mesma molécula. … Por exemplo, atualmente, a semaglutida possui registro apenas como produto biotecnológico. Portanto, não é permitida a importação nem a manipulação da semaglutida sintética até que exista um medicamento registrado com o IFA sintético." (English: "For APIs obtained by chemical synthesis, compounding is permitted provided registered medicines with the same molecule already exist in Brazil. … For example, semaglutide is currently registered only as a biotechnological product. Therefore, import and compounding of synthetic semaglutide are not permitted until a medicine with the synthetic API is registered.") · grader: research agents under the jurisdiction research brief; statements are regulatory facts, graded context

claims.text: In Brazil, ANVISA stated in Apr 2025 that its measure does not change the physician's right to prescribe medicines for purposes other than those on the label (off-label use), when the physician considers that, for a given patient, the benefits outweigh the risks.
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "A medida não altera o direito do profissional médico de prescrever medicamentos para finalidades diferentes das descritas na bula. Essa prática, conhecida como uso "off label", acontece quando o médico entende que, para determinado paciente, os benefícios do tratamento superam os riscos." (English: "The measure does not change the physician's right to prescribe medicines for purposes other than those described in the label. This practice, known as "off-label" use, occurs when the physician considers that, for a given patient, the benefits of treatment outweigh the risks.") · grader: research agents under the jurisdiction research brief; statements are regulatory facts, graded context

claims.text: In Brazil, no medicine, including an imported one, may be manufactured, sold or supplied before it is registered (Law 6.360/1976, art. 12).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "Art. 12 - Nenhum dos produtos de que trata esta Lei, inclusive os importados, poderá ser industrializado, exposto à venda ou entregue ao consumo antes de registrado no Ministério da Saúde." (English: "Art. 12 – None of the products covered by this Law, including imported ones, may be manufactured, offered for sale or supplied for consumption before being registered with the Ministry of Health.") · grader: research agents under the jurisdiction research brief; statements are regulatory facts, graded context

claims.text: In Brazil, ANVISA stated on 2 Jul 2026 that some injectable peptides are not regularised in any category (food, medicine, cosmetic or supplement) and are therefore illegal for any health use, including aesthetic use.
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "Não à toa, alguns peptídeos injetáveis NÃO estão regularizados na Agência Nacional de Vigilância Sanitária (Anvisa) em nenhuma categoria - alimento, medicamento, cosmético, suplemento alimentar -, ou seja, são ILEGAIS para qualquer uso em saúde, inclusive estético." (English: "Not surprisingly, some injectable peptides are NOT regularised with the National Health Surveillance Agency (Anvisa) in any category – food, medicine, cosmetic, food supplement – that is, they are ILLEGAL for any health use, including aesthetic use.") · grader: research agents under the jurisdiction research brief; statements are regulatory facts, graded context

claims.text: In Brazil, ANVISA stated in Jul 2026 that an investigational (experimental) medicine is used exclusively in authorised clinical research.
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "O medicamento experimental, também chamado de medicamento investigacional, é utilizado exclusivamente em pesquisas clínicas autorizadas." (English: "An experimental medicine, also called an investigational medicine, is used exclusively in authorised clinical research.") · grader: research agents under the jurisdiction research brief; statements are regulatory facts, graded context

claims.text: In Brazil, unregistered medicines may be imported only exceptionally, for strictly personal use, with a medical prescription; when ANVISA publishes a specific prohibition (as for several GLP-1 pens in 2025–2026), import by any route is suspended.
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "Medicamentos sem registro no Brasil só podem ser importados de forma excepcional e para uso exclusivamente pessoal, mediante prescrição médica e o cumprimento de requisitos adicionais. Porém, nos casos em que a Anvisa publica proibição específica, a importação, por qualquer modalidade, também fica suspensa." (English: "Medicines without registration in Brazil may only be imported exceptionally and for exclusively personal use, on medical prescription and subject to additional requirements. However, where Anvisa publishes a specific prohibition, import by any route is also suspended.") · grader: research agents under the jurisdiction research brief; statements are regulatory facts, graded context

claims.text: In Brazil, ANVISA stated in Sep 2025 that use of an unregistered imported medicine is entirely the responsibility of the patient and the prescribing physician.
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "Outro alerta: medicamentos sem registro no Brasil não tiveram sua segurança e eficácia avaliadas pela Agência. Seu uso é de inteira responsabilidade do paciente e do médico prescritor, além do risco de falsificação no mercado internacional." (English: "Another warning: medicines without registration in Brazil have not had their safety and efficacy assessed by the Agency. Their use is the entire responsibility of the patient and the prescribing physician, besides the risk of falsification on the international market.") · grader: research agents under the jurisdiction research brief; statements are regulatory facts, graded context

claims.text: In Brazil, cosmetic labelling may not carry therapeutic claims for the product or its ingredients (RDC 907/2024, art. 12), so a peptide serum that claims to treat a condition falls outside the cosmetic category.
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "Art. 12. A rotulagem não deve conter nome comercial, marcas, imagens, links eletrônicos ou dizeres que: … II - representem alegações terapêuticas atribuídas ao uso do produto ou de seus ingredientes" (English: "Art. 12. Labelling must not contain trade names, brands, images, electronic links or wording that: … II – represent therapeutic claims attributed to the use of the product or its ingredients") · grader: research agents under the jurisdiction research brief; statements are regulatory facts, graded context

claims.text: In Brazil, ANVISA stated on 2 Jul 2026 that injectable cosmetics do not exist; an injectable product offered as a cosmetic is irregular. Topical products named after GHK-Cu do appear as notified cosmetics in ANVISA's cosmetics dataset (221 entries, 25 Sep 2026); ANVISA cancelled several GHK-Cu cosmetic processes on 29 Apr 2026 without published reasons (RE 1.771/2026).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "Por fim, apesar de suposta finalidade estética, esses produtos também NÃO são cosméticos. Não existem cosméticos injetáveis e, se o produto é oferecido desta forma, trata-se de cosmético irregular." (English: "Finally, despite their supposed aesthetic purpose, these products are also NOT cosmetics. Injectable cosmetics do not exist and, if the product is offered in this form, it is an irregular cosmetic.") · grader: research agents under the jurisdiction research brief; statements are regulatory facts, graded context

claims.text: In Brazil, a food supplement is by definition a product for oral ingestion for healthy people (RDC 243/2018), so no injectable supplement can exist.
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "VII - suplemento alimentar: produto para ingestão oral, apresentado em formas farmacêuticas, destinado a suplementar a alimentação de indivíduos saudáveis com nutrientes, substâncias bioativas, enzimas ou probióticos, isolados ou combinados." (English: "VII – food supplement: a product for oral ingestion, presented in pharmaceutical forms, intended to supplement the diet of healthy individuals with nutrients, bioactive substances, enzymes or probiotics, alone or combined.") · grader: research agents under the jurisdiction research brief; statements are regulatory facts, graded context

claims.text: In Brazil, the constituents a food supplement may use are those on ANVISA's authorised list (IN 28/2018); constituents not on the list must not be used.
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "Os constituintes autorizados constam da lista aprovada na IN 28/2018 e são diferentes para os seguintes grupos etários: 0 a 3 anos (Anexo II) e acima de 3 anos (Anexo I). … Constituintes que não constem dessa lista não devem ser utilizados." (English: "Authorised constituents are on the list approved in IN 28/2018 and differ for the following age groups: 0 to 3 years (Annex II) and over 3 years (Annex I). … Constituents not on this list must not be used.") · grader: research agents under the jurisdiction research brief; statements are regulatory facts, graded context

claims.text: In Brazil, promotion of prescription-only medicines is restricted to media aimed exclusively at professionals who can prescribe or dispense them, and online promotion must sit behind a registration wall for those professionals (RDC 96/2008, arts 27 and 29).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "Art. 29 A propaganda ou publicidade de medicamentos de venda sob prescrição veiculada na internet deve ser acessível, exclusivamente, aos profissionais habilitados a prescrever ou dispensar medicamentos, por meio de sistema de cadastramento eletrônico" (English: "Art. 29 Advertising or publicity of prescription-only medicines on the internet must be accessible exclusively to professionals authorised to prescribe or dispense medicines, through an electronic registration system") · grader: research agents under the jurisdiction research brief; statements are regulatory facts, graded context

claims.text: In Brazil, compounding pharmacies may give only prescribers factual material naming active substances and referenced indications, with no brand names, prices or promotional content (RDC 96/2008, art. 36); ANVISA restated in Nov 2024 that advertising compounded products to the public is not permitted.
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "A norma também reforçou a proibição da propaganda de produtos manipulados para o público em geral, o que não é permitido na legislação atual." (English: "The rule also reinforced the prohibition on advertising compounded products to the general public, which is not permitted under current legislation.") · grader: research agents under the jurisdiction research brief; statements are regulatory facts, graded context

claims.text: In Brazil, since 23 Jun 2025 all GLP-1 agonist medicines (semaglutide, liraglutide, dulaglutide, tirzepatide and others), industrial or compounded, need a two-copy prescription valid 90 days that the pharmacy retains (RDC 973/2025 and IN 360/2025).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "A Instrução Normativa-IN nº 360 e a Resolução da Diretoria Colegiada - RDC nº 973 foram publicadas em 24 de abril de 2025, e entrarão em vigor 60 (sessenta) dias após essa data. Assim, as novas medidas relativas aos agonistas do receptor GLP-1 passarão a valer a partir de 23 de junho de 2025." (English: "Normative Instruction IN 360 and Collegiate Board Resolution RDC 973 were published on 24 April 2025 and enter into force 60 (sixty) days after that date. Thus, the new measures on GLP-1 receptor agonists apply from 23 June 2025.") · grader: research agents under the jurisdiction research brief; statements are regulatory facts, graded context

claims.text: In Brazil, the Federal Council of Medicine bars physicians from using anabolic steroids or androgens for aesthetic purposes or performance, and from prescribing hormones marketed as "bioidentical" or "nano" without proof of superiority (CFM Resolution 2.333/2023, in force since its publication on 11 Apr 2023; listed as in force on 25 Sep 2026).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "Art. 3º São vedados no exercício da Medicina, por serem destituídos de comprovação científica suficiente quanto ao seu benefício e segurança para o ser humano, o uso e a divulgação dos seguintes procedimentos: … II – Utilização de formulações de esteroides anabolizantes ou hormônios androgênicos com a finalidade estética; … IV – A prescrição de hormônios divulgados como “bioidênticos”, em formulação “nano” ou nomenclaturas de cunho comercial e sem a devida comprovação científica de superioridade clínica para a finalidade prevista nesta resolução." (English: "Art. 3 The following procedures are prohibited in medical practice, lacking sufficient scientific proof of benefit and safety for humans, as are their use and promotion: … II – Use of formulations of anabolic steroids or androgenic hormones for aesthetic purposes; … IV – The prescription of hormones promoted as “bioidentical”, in “nano” formulation or under commercial names, without due scientific proof of clinical superiority for the purpose set out in this resolution.") · grader: research agents under the jurisdiction research brief; statements are regulatory facts, graded context

claims.text: In Brazil, CFM Resolution 1.999/2012 (in force Sep 2026) bars physicians from using hormones, including growth hormone, to prevent, delay, modulate or reverse ageing, except to replace a diagnosed deficiency with proven benefit.
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "III. (English: "A Member State may, in accordance with legislation in force and to fulfil special needs, exclude from the provisions of this Directive medicinal products supplied in response to a bona fide unsolicited order, formulated in accordance with the specifications of an authorised health-care professional and for use by an individual patient under his direct personal responsibility.") · grader: research agents under the jurisdiction research brief; statements are regulatory facts, graded context

claims.text: EMA and HMA's shortage steering group asked EU prescribers in June 2024 to prescribe GLP-1 receptor agonists only for their authorised uses and said these medicines are not approved for, and should not be used for, cosmetic weight loss.
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "The MSSG therefore recommends that healthcare professionals prescribe these medicines in line with their authorised use(s) only, taking into account guidance issued by national authorities or applicable national therapeutic guidelines. GLP-1 receptor agonists are not approved for, and should not be used for, cosmetic weight loss, i.e. use for weight loss in people without obesity or people with overweight who do not have weight-related health problems." (English: "The MSSG therefore recommends that healthcare professionals prescribe these medicines in line with their authorised use(s) only, taking into account guidance issued by national authorities or applicable national therapeutic guidelines. GLP-1 receptor agonists are not approved for, and should not be used for, cosmetic weight loss, i.e. use for weight loss in people without obesity or people with overweight who do not have weight-related health problems.") · grader: research agents under the jurisdiction research brief; statements are regulatory facts, graded context

claims.text: Under EU law a product is a medicine by presentation (presented as treating or preventing disease) or by function (restoring, correcting or modifying physiological functions by a pharmacological, immunological or metabolic action), and where a product could be both a medicine and another regulated product, medicines law applies (Directive 2001/83/EC, Articles 1(2) and 2(2)).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "Any substance or combination of substances presented as having properties for treating or preventing disease in human beings; or … Any substance or combination of substances which may be used in or administered to human beings either with a view to restoring, correcting or modifying physiological functions by exerting a pharmacological, immunological or metabolic action, or to making a medical diagnosis. … In cases of doubt, where, taking into account all its characteristics, a product may fall within the definition of a ‘medicinal product’ and within the definition of a product covered by other Community legislation the provisions of this Directive shall apply." (English: "Any substance or combination of substances presented as having properties for treating or preventing disease in human beings; or … Any substance or combination of substances which may be used in or administered to human beings either with a view to restoring, correcting or modifying physiological functions by exerting a pharmacological, immunological or metabolic action, or to making a medical diagnosis. … In cases of doubt, where, taking into account all its characteristics, a product may fall within the definition of a ‘medicinal product’ and within the definition of a product covered by other Community legislation the provisions of this Directive shall apply.") · grader: research agents under the jurisdiction research brief; statements are regulatory facts, graded context

claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "Medicinal products intended for research and development trials, but without prejudice to the provisions of Directive 2001/20/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 4 April 2001 on the approximation of the laws, regulations and administrative provisions of the Member States relating to the implementation of good clinical practice in the conduct of clinical trials on medicinal products for human use" (English: "Medicinal products intended for research and development trials, but without prejudice to the provisions of Directive 2001/20/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 4 April 2001 on the approximation of the laws, regulations and administrative provisions of the Member States relating to the implementation of good clinical practice in the conduct of clinical trials on medicinal products for human use") · grader: research agents under the jurisdiction research brief; statements are regulatory facts, graded context

claims.text: On 3 September 2025 EMA and HMA warned of a sharp rise in illegal medicines sold online and on social media as GLP-1 receptor agonists (semaglutide, liraglutide, tirzepatide); these products are unauthorised and may not contain the stated substance.
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "In recent months there has been a sharp rise in the number of illegal medicines marketed as GLP-1 receptor agonists such as semaglutide, liraglutide and tirzepatide for weight loss and diabetes. These products, often sold via fraudulent websites and promoted on social media, are not authorised and do not meet necessary standards of quality, safety and efficacy. … They may not contain the claimed active substance at all and may contain harmful levels of other substances." (English: "In recent months there has been a sharp rise in the number of illegal medicines marketed as GLP-1 receptor agonists such as semaglutide, liraglutide and tirzepatide for weight loss and diabetes. These products, often sold via fraudulent websites and promoted on social media, are not authorised and do not meet necessary standards of quality, safety and efficacy. … They may not contain the claimed active substance at all and may contain harmful levels of other substances.") · grader: research agents under the jurisdiction research brief; statements are regulatory facts, graded context

claims.text: In the EU, anything intended to be ingested, inhaled, injected or implanted is not a cosmetic (Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009, Article 2(2)), so an injected peptide can never be a cosmetic.
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "a substance or mixture intended to be ingested, inhaled, injected or implanted into the human body shall not be considered to be a cosmetic product" (English: "a substance or mixture intended to be ingested, inhaled, injected or implanted into the human body shall not be considered to be a cosmetic product") · grader: research agents under the jurisdiction research brief; statements are regulatory facts, graded context

claims.text: The EU borderline manual (version 5.4, November 2024, retained in 5.5) says a product in a vial or ampoule for injection cannot be a cosmetic, and one sold as a cosmetic must be clearly for external use and not marketed with a device allowing injection or delivery below the epidermis.
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "If a substance or mixture presented in a vial or ampoule is for use by injection, then the product cannot be considered to meet the definition of a cosmetic product by virtue of Article 2(2) of the Cosmetics Regulation … Furthermore, the product should not be marketed with a device which could allow the injection of this product or its delivery below the epidermis" (English: "If a substance or mixture presented in a vial or ampoule is for use by injection, then the product cannot be considered to meet the definition of a cosmetic product by virtue of Article 2(2) of the Cosmetics Regulation … Furthermore, the product should not be marketed with a device which could allow the injection of this product or its delivery below the epidermis") · grader: research agents under the jurisdiction research brief; statements are regulatory facts, graded context

claims.text: Whether an EU product is a cosmetic is decided case by case by national authorities; the borderline manual says an anti-wrinkle product that significantly restores, corrects or modifies physiological functions by a pharmacological, immunological or metabolic action does not qualify as a cosmetic (June 2025).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "However, some products presented as anti -wrinkle may significantly restore, correct or modify physiological functions by exerting a pharmacological, immunological or metabolic action. In that case, they would not qualify as cosmetics. … A decision on the qualification of the products has to be made by the na tional competent authorities on a case -by-case basis" (English: "However, some products presented as anti -wrinkle may significantly restore, correct or modify physiological functions by exerting a pharmacological, immunological or metabolic action. In that case, they would not qualify as cosmetics. … A decision on the qualification of the products has to be made by the na tional competent authorities on a case -by-case basis") · grader: research agents under the jurisdiction research brief; statements are regulatory facts, graded context

claims.text: Before an EU cosmetic is placed on the market it needs a responsible person in the EU, a safety assessment with a cosmetic product safety report, and electronic notification to the Commission (Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009, Articles 4, 10 and 13).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "Only cosmetic products for which a legal or natural person is designated within the Community as ‘responsible person’ shall be placed on the market. … the responsible person shall, prior to placing a cosmetic product on the market, ensure that the cosmetic product has undergone a safety assessment on the basis of the relevant information and that a cosmetic product safety report is set up in accordance with Annex I. … Prior to placing the cosmetic product on the market the responsible person shall submit, by electronic means, the following information to the Commission" (English: "Only cosmetic products for which a legal or natural person is designated within the Community as ‘responsible person’ shall be placed on the market. … the responsible person shall, prior to placing a cosmetic product on the market, ensure that the cosmetic product has undergone a safety assessment on the basis of the relevant information and that a cosmetic product safety report is set up in accordance with Annex I. … Prior to placing the cosmetic product on the market the responsible person shall submit, by electronic means, the following information to the Commission") · grader: research agents under the jurisdiction research brief; statements are regulatory facts, graded context

claims.text: EU cosmetic claims must be supported by adequate and verifiable evidence, and a claim that extrapolates an ingredient's properties (for example a peptide's) to the finished product needs evidence such as the ingredient's presence at an effective concentration (Regulation (EU) No 655/2013).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "Claims for cosmetic products, whether explicit or implicit, shall be supported by adequate and verifiable evidence regardless of the types of evidential support used to substantiate them, including where appropriate expert assessments. … A claim extrapolating (explicitly or implicitly) ingredient properties to the finished product shall be supported by adequate and verifiable evidence, such as by demonstrating the presence of the ingredient at an effective concentration." (English: "Claims for cosmetic products, whether explicit or implicit, shall be supported by adequate and verifiable evidence regardless of the types of evidential support used to substantiate them, including where appropriate expert assessments. … A claim extrapolating (explicitly or implicitly) ingredient properties to the finished product shall be supported by adequate and verifiable evidence, such as by demonstrating the presence of the ingredient at an effective concentration.") · grader: research agents under the jurisdiction research brief; statements are regulatory facts, graded context

claims.text: In the EU, food supplements are foods that supplement the normal diet, are concentrated sources of nutrients or other substances with a nutritional or physiological effect, and are sold in measured doses such as capsules, tablets or sachets (Directive 2002/46/EC, Article 2(a)).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "‘food supplements’ means foodstuffs the purpose of which is to supplement the normal diet and which are concentrated sources of nutrients or other substances with a nutritional or physiological effect, alone or in combination, marketed in dose form, namely forms such as capsules, pastilles, tablets, pills and other similar forms, sachets of powder, ampoules of liquids, drop dispensing bottles, and other similar forms of liquids and powders designed to be taken in measured small unit quantities" (English: "‘food supplements’ means foodstuffs the purpose of which is to supplement the normal diet and which are concentrated sources of nutrients or other substances with a nutritional or physiological effect, alone or in combination, marketed in dose form, namely forms such as capsules, pastilles, tablets, pills and other similar forms, sachets of powder, ampoules of liquids, drop dispensing bottles, and other similar forms of liquids and powders designed to be taken in measured small unit quantities") · grader: research agents under the jurisdiction research brief; statements are regulatory facts, graded context

claims.text: In the EU, a health claim on a food is prohibited unless it is authorised and included in the EU lists of authorised claims (Regulation (EC) No 1924/2006, Article 10(1)).
claims.reviewNote: primary source quote: "Health claims shall be prohibited unless they comply with the general requirements in Chapter II and the specific requirements in this Chapter and are authorised in accordance with this Regulation and included in the lists of authorised claims provided for in Articles 13 and 14." claims.text: In the EU, food information, including advertising, must not attribute to any food the property of preventing, treating or curing a human disease (Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011, Article 7(3) and (4)).

claims.text: EU law requires member states to prohibit advertising of prescription-only medicines to the general public (Directive 2001/83/EC, Article 88(1)(a)); 'advertising' includes any inducement designed to promote prescription, supply, sale or consumption (Article 86(1)).

claims.text: EU audiovisual law bans audiovisual commercial communications for prescription-only medicines and medical treatment, and video-sharing platforms must take measures to apply this to advertising on their services, including advertising they do not sell themselves (Directive 2010/13/EU, Articles 9(1)(f) and 28b(2)).

claims.text: In Portugal, compounded medicines may only use raw materials listed in the Portuguese or European pharmacopoeia, another European pharmacopoeia or compendial scientific documentation, and a compounded medicine containing any other raw material may not be prescribed (Decreto-Lei 95/2004, Art 6).
