units.tutorContext: Module 3 teaches metabolic and adipose influences on facial architecture in four separate registers (mechanism, human evidence, regulatory status, open question). dWAT: distinct adipocyte layer in the reticular dermis; reactive adipogenesis and cathelicidin against S. aureus and its age-related loss via TGF-β are mouse data (D); human dWAT is cone-shaped around follicles and human acne lesions contain cathelicidin-producing preadipocytes (D); its role in human skin ageing is unmeasured. Facial subcutaneous fat sits in discrete compartments (cadaver anatomy); in 186 identical-twin pairs higher BMI looked older before ~40 and younger after (C, observational). Glycation: AGEs accumulate in human skin collagen (~5-fold from 20 to 85 y, up to 2x in type 1 diabetes; skin collagen half-life ~15 y) — C; AGE cross-links and RAGE–NF-κB causing visible ageing: the Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology guide rates B, the course grades D (lab/animal + associations); skin autofluorescence is a surrogate validated in non-pigmented skin; 'anti-glycation' products are tested on surrogates or appearance scores (guide grade C). Incretins: semaglutide (GLP-1 RA) and tirzepatide (GIP/GLP-1 RA). US status Sept 2026: Ozempic (T2D, 2017) and Wegovy (weight 06/2021; adolescents 12/2022; CV risk reduction 03/2024; MASH F2–F3 accelerated 08/2025); Mounjaro (T2D, 2022) and Zepbound (weight 11/2023; OSA 12/2024). Compounded, counterfeit and 'research' versions are not FDA-approved. STEP-1 −14.9% vs −2.4% (68 wk); SURMOUNT-1 −15.0 to −20.9% vs −3.1% (72 wk) — GRADE A for weight; median ~28% of weight lost is muscle-related (35 RCTs, B). Facial change ('Ozempic face'): retrospective imaging n=20, median 9% midface volume loss, mostly superficial, ~7%/10 kg (D); survey n=1,226, sagging/facial volume loss/hair loss rise with % weight lost (C); no RCT has measured the face; direct drug action on facial fat is a cell-study hypothesis. US labels list hair loss (~3–6% vs ~1% placebo, mostly women, linked to weight reduction) but not facial volume loss. Practice: counsel before treatment, photograph with consent, protect lean mass (protein, resistance training — no figures), refer restoration to a qualified aesthetic clinician; restoration advice is industry-linked expert consensus; decisions about stopping or changing the medicine belong to the prescriber and patient — never advise stopping, switching or dosing. Gut: inflammaging (IL-6/CRP predict frailty, death); metabolic endotoxaemia shown in mice and as a transient rise after a fatty meal in 12 men (D); restoring barrier function unproven for disease outside the gut; commercial zonulin ELISA detects other proteins. Probiotics for eczema: Cochrane 39 RCTs little/no patient-rated difference (B); children's meta-analysis small SCORAD gain (C). Rifaximin for rosacea with SIBO: small RCT (C). Tirzepatide + ixekizumab psoriasis: open-label Lilly phase 3b (C); liraglutide 20-person RCT negative (C); tirzepatide not approved for psoriasis in the US. Fibre: strong cardiometabolic evidence (guide grade A; review certainty moderate), no skin trials. Akkermansia pilot RCT metabolic only (C). 'Leaky gut' repair stack incl. BPC-157: guide grade D; BPC-157 not on the 503A bulks list (Sept 2026). Adapt the 'what you do next' to the learner's role (prescriber, clinical staff, advisor) without changing grades or regulatory facts. UK (checked 25 Sep 2026): Ozempic licensed for T2D; Wegovy for weight management and CV risk reduction; Mounjaro for T2D and weight management under one brand (weight added 8 Nov 2023); UK SmPCs list hair loss (Wegovy 2.5%, Mounjaro 4.9% vs 1.0%); psoriasis not a UK tirzepatide indication; MHRA: retatrutide not authorised, illegal to sell (24 Jul 2026); largest seizure of unlicensed weight-loss medicines 28 May 2026; unlicensed 'specials' only for one patient's special clinical need, on the prescriber's responsibility (MHRA GN14). No CME credit is currently offered.

videoTranscript.en: Facial shape depends on fat as much as on collagen. In three lessons you will separate what is known about the skin's own fat, sugar damage to the dermis, weight-loss drugs and the gut from what is still mechanism, marketing or an open question. Most people picture skin fat as one layer under the dermis. There is a second, thinner layer inside the reticular dermis itself, called dermal white adipose tissue. In mice, this layer expands rapidly after a Staphylococcus aureus infection, and its new fat cells release cathelicidin, an antimicrobial peptide. Older mice lose much of that capacity, through TGF-beta signalling. Human skin arranges this fat differently, in small cones around hair follicles, and human acne lesions contain preadipocytes around the follicle that make cathelicidin. What the layer contributes to human skin ageing has not yet been measured. So hold two things apart when you hear about skin fat. The defence story is strong in mice and emerging in people. The ageing story in people is still a proposal.

title.en: The skin keeps its own fat.

body.en: Beneath the dermis lies subcutaneous fat. Within the reticular dermis itself sits a thinner layer, dermal white adipose tissue. In mice, this layer expands rapidly after a Staphylococcus aureus infection, its new fat cells release the antimicrobial peptide cathelicidin, and the capacity fades with age through TGF-β signalling. Human skin arranges this fat differently, in cones around hair follicles, and human acne lesions contain perifollicular preadipocytes that make cathelicidin. What the layer contributes to human skin ageing has not been measured.

points.en: A second fat layer inside the dermis
In mice: antimicrobial, and lost with age
In people: a different shape, and an open question about ageing

body.en: Dermal white adipose tissue sits inside the reticular dermis, separate from the subcutaneous fat below. Fat as a whole is an endocrine organ that releases hormones such as leptin and adiponectin.
The layer expands after skin infection and its fat cells release cathelicidin. Older mice lose much of this capacity, through TGF-β signalling.
Human dermal fat clusters in cones around hair follicles, and acne lesions contain preadipocytes that make cathelicidin. Its part in skin ageing is unmeasured.

title.en: Fat that holds the face up.

body.en: Cadaver dissection shows that the face's subcutaneous fat sits in separate compartments, and facial ageing is partly how each compartment changes. Weight shows the same thing from the outside. In a study of 186 pairs of identical twins, the twin with the higher body-mass index looked older before about age 40 and younger after it.

detail.en: Guyuron et al., 2009 — a four-point higher BMI tracked with an older look before about 40 and a younger look after it

means.en: From midlife on, facial fat goes with a younger-looking face. That fits the anatomy: the face ages partly as its fat compartments change. GRADE C, observational.

doesNot.en: It is an observational comparison of photographs. It does not show that gaining weight rejuvenates, or that fat loss on a drug changes the skin itself.

body.en: Glycation is a slow, non-enzymatic reaction. Reducing sugars attach to protein amino groups, rearrange into Amadori products and end as advanced glycation end products, or AGEs. On long-lived dermal collagen, AGEs form cross-links that stiffen the matrix. Through their receptor, RAGE, AGEs switch on inflammatory signalling in laboratory studies. The Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology guide rates the structural and inflammatory effects B; the course grades the causal link to visible ageing D, because the human data are associations.

points.en: Sugar + protein → Schiff base → Amadori product → AGE
Cross-links stiffen long-lived collagen
RAGE signalling: shown in the laboratory

blocks.sourceNote: Gkogkolou & Böhm 2012 · Dyer 1993 · Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology, ch. 13

body.en: Reducing sugars bind protein amino groups, form a reversible Schiff base, then a more stable Amadori product, and finally irreversible AGEs.
Structural: AGEs cross-link collagen and elastin and stiffen the dermis. Signalling: AGEs bind RAGE, which drives NF-κB and inflammatory cytokines in cell and animal studies.
The Hormonaly endocrinology guide rates both B. The course grades the causal link to visible ageing D, because the human data are associations.

audioScript.en: Glycation is chemistry before it is biology. Reducing sugars attach to the amino groups of proteins, rearrange into more stable products, and end as advanced glycation end products, known as AGEs. Dermal collagen lasts for years, so it collects AGEs, and they form cross-links that make the matrix stiffer. AGEs also bind a receptor called RAGE, which in laboratory studies switches on inflammatory signalling and enzymes that break down matrix. Keep the registers apart here. The chemistry, and the build-up of AGEs in human skin, are well documented. The idea that AGEs cause the wrinkles and laxity you see in clinic rests on laboratory and animal work plus human associations. The Aesthetic and Regenerative Endocrinology guide rates the structural and inflammatory effects grade B. This course grades the causal link D, and the next moment shows why.

title.en: Fifteen years on the same collagen.

body.en: Human skin collagen turns over slowly; tissue analysis puts its half-life at about 15 years. In skin biopsies, glycoxidation products in collagen rose about five-fold between ages 20 and 85, and were up to twice as high in type 1 diabetes. Skin autofluorescence, a non-invasive reading, correlates moderately with those biopsy measures and was validated in non-pigmented skin.

doesNot.en: It does not show how much of visible ageing AGEs cause, or that any product reverses established cross-links. Skin autofluorescence is a surrogate reading of AGE load.

prompt.en: Tap what stands behind each statement.

label.en: Dermal fat cells release cathelicidin to fight Staphylococcus aureus

why.en: Shown in mouse infection models (D). Human acne lesions contain preadipocytes that make cathelicidin, but protection against infection has not been tested in people.

label.en: Dermal fat loses its defensive capacity with age

why.en: Shown in mice, through TGF-β signalling (D). The equivalent change in human skin has not been measured.

label.en: AGEs build up in skin collagen with age, faster in diabetes

why.en: Measured directly in human skin biopsies (C, observational), and up to twice as high in type 1 diabetes.

label.en: Skin collagen stays in place for many years

why.en: Human tissue analysis puts the half-life of skin collagen at about 15 years (C), which is why glycation damage accumulates.

label.en: AGEs drive skin inflammation through their receptor, RAGE

why.en: Laboratory and animal work. The Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology guide rates it B; the course grades the causal link D because the human data are associations.

label.en: An anti-glycation serum reverses cross-linked collagen

why.en: Not shown. Trials of 'anti-glycation' products measure surrogate readings or appearance scores; none found for this course measured cross-links in human skin. The guide rates the evidence for these products C, on surrogate endpoints.

done.en: Six sorted. Two are measured in human skin, three come from mice or cells, and one has no study behind it.

body.en: GLP-1 and GIP are incretins, hormones the gut releases after a meal that amplify glucose-dependent insulin release; GLP-1 also slows gastric emptying and reduces appetite. Native GLP-1 is broken down within minutes. Semaglutide is a long-acting GLP-1 receptor agonist, and tirzepatide activates both GIP and GLP-1 receptors. In the US, as of September 2026, both are FDA-approved drugs for defined indications, set out in the next moment.

points.en: Incretins amplify insulin after meals
Semaglutide: GLP-1 receptor agonist
Tirzepatide: GIP and GLP-1 receptor agonist

body.en: GLP-1 from intestinal L-cells and GIP from K-cells amplify insulin release when glucose is high. GLP-1 also slows the stomach and reduces appetite.
Native GLP-1 is cleared within minutes by the enzyme DPP-4. The drug molecules are modified to last far longer in the blood.
In the US, semaglutide is sold as Ozempic and Wegovy, tirzepatide as Mounjaro and Zepbound, and the brand tells you the approved use.

audioScript.en: After a meal, the gut releases two hormones called incretins, GLP-1 and GIP. Both amplify insulin release when glucose is high, and GLP-1 also slows the stomach and reduces appetite. Native GLP-1 lasts only minutes in the blood before an enzyme breaks it down, so the drug molecules are engineered to last far longer. Semaglutide activates the GLP-1 receptor. Tirzepatide activates both the GIP and the GLP-1 receptors. Those are the mechanisms. The regulatory facts sit in a separate register. In the United States, as of September 2026, both molecules are FDA-approved drugs, sold under one brand name for type 2 diabetes and another for chronic weight management, with further indications for the heart, the liver and sleep apnoea. The face appears nowhere on those labels, and that is where this lesson begins.

text.en: In the UK both are licensed by the MHRA, and tirzepatide's diabetes and weight-management uses share one brand, Mounjaro.

In the EU, semaglutide is a centrally authorised prescription medicine, as Ozempic and Rybelsus for diabetes and Wegovy for weight management (EMA and HMA, June 2024), and tirzepatide is authorised as Mounjaro (EU-wide, 15 September 2022) for diabetes and adult weight management, prescription-only. A search of the Union Register and EMA's medicines data on 25 September 2026 found no EU product named Zepbound.

In Brazil, ANVISA has registered semaglutide as Ozempic (since 6 August 2018) and Wegovy (since 2 January 2023), with synthetic semaglutide pens registered from 26 May 2026, and tirzepatide as Mounjaro (since 25 September 2023); a search of its register on 25 September 2026 found no product named Zepbound. Since 23 June 2025, GLP-1 receptor agonist medicines may only be sold with retention of the prescription (RDC 973/2025 and IN 360/2025).

In the UAE, the Emirates Drug Establishment (EDE) has been the federal authority regulating medical products since Federal Decree-Law 28/2023, and its register lists semaglutide as Ozempic, Rybelsus and Wegovy and tirzepatide as Mounjaro; every entry checked is a Prescription Only Medicine. A search of the EDE register on 25 September 2026 found no product named Zepbound.

body.en: The facial changes in this lesson happen to people taking approved drugs for approved reasons. Know the indications, and their dates, before you discuss the side effects. Status below is for the US, from FDA records checked in September 2026.

blocks.sourceNote: US labels via DailyMed (2026) · Drugs@FDA · FDA, current 1 Sep 2026 · Ashraf 2024

note.en: First approved 2017. The label adds cardiovascular and kidney risk reduction in people with type 2 diabetes.

Approved June 2021; adolescents from age 12 added December 2022. Cardiovascular risk reduction in established heart disease with obesity or overweight, March 2024. MASH with moderate to advanced liver fibrosis, accelerated approval, August 2025.
First approved 2022. The label adds cardiovascular risk reduction in type 2 diabetes at high risk.
Approved November 2023. Moderate to severe obstructive sleep apnoea with obesity, December 2024.

FDA warns about compounded, counterfeit and falsely labelled 'research' semaglutide and tirzepatide (page current 1 September 2026). Semaglutide bought online without a prescription has failed independent testing.

callout.en: Approved for diabetes, weight, the heart, the liver and sleep apnoea. The face is on none of these labels.

text.en: In the UK (MHRA, September 2026), Ozempic is licensed for diabetes and Mounjaro for diabetes and weight. Wegovy is licensed for weight management and cardiovascular risk reduction; MHRA added weight management to Mounjaro in November 2023. MHRA says retatrutide is not authorised in the UK and anyone selling it does so illegally (24 July 2026), and in May 2026 it made its largest seizure of unlicensed weight-loss medicines.

In the EU, semaglutide is authorised as Ozempic for diabetes (since 8 February 2018) and Wegovy for weight management (since 6 January 2022), and tirzepatide as Mounjaro for diabetes and adult weight management (since 15 September 2022), all prescription-only. In June 2024 EMA and HMA's shortage steering group said GLP-1 receptor agonists are not approved for, and should not be used for, cosmetic weight loss, and on 3 September 2025 EMA and HMA warned of a sharp rise in illegal medicines sold online and on social media as semaglutide, liraglutide or tirzepatide, which are unauthorised and may not contain the stated substance.

In Portugal, Wegovy and Mounjaro are authorised through the EU centralised procedure and are prescription-only, and on 4 July 2024 INFARMED stated that Ozempic, Trulicity and Victoza must not be prescribed to patients who are not diabetic (Circular 045/CD/100.20.200). In September 2025 INFARMED relayed the EMA and HMA warning of a sharp increase in the illegal marketing of medicines presented as GLP-1 receptor agonists, and stated that in Portugal medicines can only be bought on the internet from the websites of pharmacies and licensed non-prescription medicine outlets (LVMNSRM).

In Brazil, as of September 2026, Ozempic is indicated for adults with insufficiently controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus, Wegovy is indicated for weight management in adults, Mounjaro is indicated for chronic weight management in adults, and the approved synthetic semaglutide copies are indicated for adult patients with insufficiently controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus. Nota Técnica 200/2025 (August 2025) permits compounding of chemically synthesised APIs provided registered medicines with the same molecule already exist in Brazil, and ANVISA inspections from January to April 2026 led to the closure of 8 of the 26 establishments assessed and the seizure of more than 1.3 million units of irregular injectable medicines.

In the UAE, the Emirates Drug Establishment (EDE) announced on 1 June 2026 that it had approved oral Wegovy (semaglutide) for long-term weight management in adults with obesity, or overweight with weight-related conditions, and a Ministry of Health and Prevention alert (Circular 9217/2024, October 2024) described genuine Mounjaro as registered for type 2 diabetes and weight management. Federal Decree-Law 38/2024 bars compounding pharmacies from compounding essential copies of products that hold an EDE marketing approval unless no commercially available product can deliver the expected benefit to the patient. On 20 July 2026 the EDE warned that 1,659 packs of Mounjaro and Ozempic missing from a warehouse are outside the legitimate supply chain and told the public to buy these medicines only from licensed pharmacies.

title.en: Large trials, measured on the scale.

body.en: In STEP-1, 1,961 adults without diabetes lost a mean 14.9% of body weight on semaglutide over 68 weeks, against 2.4% on placebo. In SURMOUNT-1, 2,539 adults lost 15.0% to 20.9% on tirzepatide over 72 weeks, depending on dose, against 3.1% on placebo. Both Hormonaly guides grade weight management A. Across 35 randomized trials of incretin drugs, a median of about 28% of the weight lost was muscle-related tissue.

note.en: One imaging study of 20 patients found a median 9% loss of midface volume, mostly superficial, about 7% per 10 kg lost. A survey of 1,226 patients found sagging, facial volume loss and hair shedding reported more often the more weight was lost. A systematic review of the plastic-surgery literature found it limited by study bias. No randomized trial has measured the face.

Whether these drugs act on facial fat or skin cells beyond the effect of weight loss rests on cell studies and has not been tested in people.

callout.en: So far, the evidence ties facial change to how much weight is lost.

text.en: UK product information also lists hair loss: 2.5% on Wegovy and 4.9% on Mounjaro in the weight-management trials, against 1.0% on placebo.

title.en: Counsel before, record during, refer when asked.

body.en: Raise facial volume change and hair shedding before treatment starts; the Hormonaly guide advises this especially for older patients. During treatment, photograph the face with consent, and support the protein intake and resistance training the guide recommends to protect lean mass. When a patient wants the face restored, refer to a qualified aesthetic or dermatology colleague. Published advice on restoration is expert opinion, the main consensus statement was developed with industry involvement, and randomized trials of fillers and devices in these patients are registered without results. Decisions about the medicine itself stay with the prescriber and the patient.

audioScript.en: Three moments matter in practice. Before treatment starts, raise facial volume change and hair shedding as possibilities, especially with older patients, as the Hormonaly guide advises, and record that you did. During treatment, photograph the face with consent so that change is measured rather than remembered, and support the protein intake and resistance training the guide recommends to protect lean mass. When a patient asks for help with the face, refer to a qualified aesthetic or dermatology colleague. The published advice on restoring volume after drug-driven weight loss is expert opinion, the main consensus statement was developed with industry involvement, and randomized trials of fillers and devices in these patients are registered with no results yet. Whatever your role, decisions about the medicine itself stay with the prescriber and the patient.

prescriber.en: Put facial volume change and hair shedding into the consent conversation before you start, and document it. At follow-up, review nutrition, strength training and consented photographs. Keep the indication in view, and refer restoration requests rather than improvising them.

clinical-staff.en: Record the patient's concern, the medicine and who prescribes it, and consented photographs. Do not suggest pausing or changing the medicine; bring the concern to the prescriber and pass restoration questions to the aesthetic lead.

advisor.en: Explain that facial change tracks the weight lost and that hair loss is a listed side effect. Questions about the dose or about stopping belong with the prescriber; restoration questions belong with a qualified aesthetic clinician.

body.en: Inflammaging is the chronic, low-grade, sterile inflammation that rises with age. In older adults, higher IL-6 and CRP predict frailty and death. One proposed source is the gut. In mice, a high-fat diet raises circulating bacterial lipopolysaccharide, and infusing it reproduces weight gain and insulin resistance. In 12 healthy men, a single high-fat meal raised plasma endotoxin within four hours. Whether a leaky gut drives skin disease in people has not been shown.

Metabolic endotoxaemia: gut bacterial LPS in the blood
Gut to skin in people: not shown

body.en: A slow rise in background inflammation with age. Higher IL-6 and CRP predict frailty, disability and death in older adults.
Bacterial lipopolysaccharide crossing a leaky barrier is one proposed source, shown in mice and as a short rise after a fatty meal in a small human study.
Measuring gut permeability is hard, and restoring the barrier has not been shown to improve disease outside the gut.

audioScript.en: Ageing brings a slow rise in background inflammation, called inflammaging. It is low-grade and sterile, and in older adults higher IL-6 and C-reactive protein predict frailty, disability and death. One proposed source is the gut. In mice, a high-fat diet raises bacterial lipopolysaccharide in the blood, and infusing that endotoxin reproduces weight gain and insulin resistance. In twelve healthy men, a single high-fat meal raised plasma endotoxin within four hours. That is the mechanism usually called metabolic endotoxaemia, or leaky gut. The human evidence stops short of the skin. Measuring gut permeability is difficult, and a leading review concludes that it is still unproven whether restoring the barrier improves disease outside the gut. Hold that line as you look at what patients are sold.

title.en: Thirty-nine trials of probiotics for eczema.

body.en: An independent Cochrane review pooled 39 randomized trials, with 2,599 participants, of oral probiotics for eczema. Probiotics probably make little or no difference to patient-rated symptoms, and investigator-rated severity fell by less than the minimum clinically important difference. A 2024 European task-force meta-analysis in children without food allergy reported a significant fall in severity scores.

blocks.sourceNote: Makrgeorgou 2018 (Cochrane) · Vassilopoulou 2024 · Suez 2019

label.en: in the Cochrane review of oral probiotics for treating eczema

detail.en: 2,599 participants · little or no difference in patient-rated symptoms (moderate-certainty evidence)

means.en: The most direct test of 'treat the gut, help the skin' in a common inflammatory skin disease shows, at most, a small effect. GRADE B for little or no benefit a patient would notice.

doesNot.en: It does not rule out benefit from particular strains or in particular groups, and it says nothing about skin ageing. Newer pooled analyses in children report small improvements.

why.en: One open-label, manufacturer-funded phase 3b trial of 274 people: more complete clearance with the add-on at 36 weeks (C). An earlier 20-person placebo-controlled trial of liraglutide found no effect. Its US approval and its UK licence both leave out psoriasis.
Strong human evidence for heart and metabolic outcomes; the guide grades it A, and the review behind it rates certainty moderate. No trial has measured skin.
One pilot randomized trial in 32 adults improved insulin sensitivity (C). No skin outcomes.

text.en: In the EU, tirzepatide is authorised as Mounjaro (EU-wide, 15 September 2022) for adult weight management, prescription-only. A search of the Union Register and EMA's data on authorised, refused and withdrawn medicines on 25 September 2026 found no centrally authorised medicine containing BPC-157.

In Brazil, Mounjaro (tirzepatide), registered by ANVISA since 25 September 2023, is indicated as an adjunct to a low-calorie diet and increased physical activity for chronic weight management in adults. ANVISA stated on 2 July 2026 that BPC-157 is not authorised for use as a food supplement and that no company applications or studies have been submitted to regularise it as a food supplement.

In the UAE, a search of the Emirates Drug Establishment (EDE) register on 25 September 2026 found no registered product containing BPC-157, and a Ministry of Health and Prevention alert (Circular 9217/2024) described genuine Mounjaro (tirzepatide) as registered for type 2 diabetes and weight management. In Dubai, the DHA prohibits prescribing, dispensing, administering or using any peptide product unless it is registered or licensed with the EDE and used within the scope of its licence (29 July 2026). In Abu Dhabi, the DoH treats peptides as high-risk substances that may be compounded only if monographed, part of an approved medicine or listed by the DoH for compounding (August 2026).

body.en: When a patient links their skin to their gut, start with what has evidence: diet quality, treating metabolic disease directly, and established treatment for the skin condition itself. A widely used commercial zonulin assay has been shown to detect proteins other than zonulin, so a result cannot tell you whether a gut is leaky. Restoring barrier function has not been shown to improve disease outside the gut. Investigational peptides sold for gut repair come last, if at all.

Zonulin tests may not measure zonulin
Gut-repair peptides: last, if at all

audioScript.en: Patients often link their skin to their gut. Start where the evidence is. Diet quality, treatment of metabolic disease and the established treatment for the skin condition itself all come first. Be careful with tests. A widely used commercial zonulin assay was shown to detect proteins other than zonulin, so a result cannot tell you whether a gut is leaky. Be careful with products too. Probiotics are strain-specific, and their effects on eczema are small at best. The Hormonaly guide gives the popular gut-repair stack of glutamine, zinc carnosine and BPC-157 a grade of D. As of September 2026, in the United States, BPC-157 remains off the 503A bulks list after the July advisory-committee review. Investigational peptides come last, if at all. Whatever your role, name the evidence type before you name the product.

prescriber.en: Treat the skin disease on its own evidence and metabolic disease directly. A zonulin result should not guide care. In the US, BPC-157 has no 503A bulks-list standing as of September 2026, so compounding it for gut repair is not an option.

clinical-staff.en: If a patient brings a gut-repair kit or a zonulin result, record the products and the result and bring them to the prescriber. Do not interpret the test or advise on the products.

advisor.en: You can say that fibre-rich diets have strong evidence for metabolic health, that probiotics are strain-specific with small skin effects at best, and that injected or research peptides need a prescriber.

text.en: In the United Kingdom, an unlicensed peptide reaches a patient only through narrow routes, such as a special ordered for one patient's clinical need, which module seven sets out.

In the EU, Directive 2001/83/EC allows a medicine on the market only with a national or EU-wide marketing authorisation (Article 6(1)), while medicines prepared in a pharmacy for an individual patient on prescription (magistral formulas) fall outside the directive and need no marketing authorisation under it (Article 3). Each member state may also, under its own law, allow an unauthorised medicine for an individual patient on a bona fide unsolicited order from an authorised health professional, under that professional's direct personal responsibility (Article 5(1)).

In Portugal, no medicine containing BPC-157 is listed in INFARMED's Infomed register (25 September 2026). A medicine is defined as any substance or combination of substances presented as having properties for treating or preventing disease or that may be used or administered to restore, correct, or modify physiological functions through pharmacological, immunological, or metabolic action (Estatuto do Medicamento, Article 3). INFARMED does not authorise importing medicines for personal use, and a compounded medicine may use only raw materials listed in the Portuguese Pharmacopoeia, the European Pharmacopoeia, pharmacopoeias of other States Parties to the European Pharmacopoeia Convention, or compendial scientific documentation (Decreto-Lei 95/2004, Article 6).

In Brazil, ANVISA stated on 2 July 2026 that any substance must have undergone efficacy and safety assessments before it can be compounded, and that some injectable peptides are not regularised in any category (food, medicine, cosmetic or food supplement) and are illegal for any health use, including aesthetic use. ANVISA also stated in July 2026 that an investigational medicine is used exclusively in authorised clinical research.

In the UAE, Federal Decree-Law 38/2024, in force since 2 January 2025, bars importing, selling or using any medical product without a marketing approval from the Emirates Drug Establishment (EDE), and lets a physician prescribe a medicine never submitted for approval only when necessary, when no equivalent alternative is available and with the patient's approval. In Dubai, the DHA prohibits using any research-use peptide on humans, or for treatment, outside a study or clinical trial approved by the competent authority (29 July 2026). In Abu Dhabi, the DoH lets physicians prescribe peptide therapies only for clinical indications supported by available scientific evidence, after a documented eligibility assessment and with informed consent that covers the product's regulatory approval status, and compounded peptides may use only certified active ingredients imported under EDE oversight (31 July 2026).

units.tutorContext: Module 4 teaches evidence appraisal of skin peptides in four separate registers (mechanism, human evidence, regulatory status, open question). Topical GHK-Cu: plausible copper-enzyme mechanism from originator reviews; one indexed RCT (Miller 2006, post-laser healing) plus sponsor-run cosmetic trials; GRADE C; injectable use has no RCTs and commonly irritates; US 503A Category 1 for non-injectable routes only (FDA list 14 May 2026; PCAC consultation planned by end Feb 2027). pal-KTTKS and Argireline: C (sponsor RCTs plus independent Aruan 2023); Matrixyl 3000, SNAP-8, Leuphasyl: D (no randomized trial; manufacturer data, plus one small uncontrolled university volunteer study for Leuphasyl). Oral collagen: pooled RCTs positive but Myung 2025 finds no effect in unfunded or high-quality trials; dietary supplement in the US. BPC-157: rodent + case series, no published human efficacy RCT (Sept 2026); TB-500 is the Tβ4 17-23 fragment, never trialled; KPV mouse colitis only; LL-37 small positive RCT then negative phase IIb. PCAC reviewed BPC-157/KPV/TB-500 in July 2026 — advisory only; not on the 503A bulks list. UK (checked 25 Sep 2026): peptide serums are cosmetics under the assimilated Cosmetics Regulation 1223/2009 (responsible person, safety assessment, OPSS notification, substantiated claims; anything injected is outside cosmetics law; ASA 13 May 2026 upheld a complaint against a peptide serum's 'clinically proven' lift claim); oral collagen is a food supplement (no disease claims; only authorised GB health claims); a medicine without a UK marketing authorisation may not be sold, supplied or advertised (HMR 2012 regs 46, 279); unlicensed 'specials' only for one patient's special need (MHRA GN14). Never give doses, stacks, reconstitution or sourcing advice; name the route and the grade; route injected or research-use-only products to a prescriber; adapt the 'what you do next' to the learner's role (prescriber, clinical staff, advisor) without changing grades or regulatory facts. No CME credit is currently offered.

learningObjectives.en: Assess the clinical trial evidence and cellular mechanisms of GHK-Cu in fibroblast stimulation, matrix metalloproteinase regulation, and wound remodeling.

Evaluate the human trial evidence, funding sources and delivery limits for topical signal peptides (pal-KTTKS), oral collagen peptides and SNAP-25 mimics (Argireline, SNAP-8, Leuphasyl), and explain why pooled benefit can disappear in independent trials.
Contrast preclinical wound-healing data with the lack of controlled human safety and efficacy trials for investigational agents including BPC-157, TB-500, and KPV.

body.en: Most skin peptides reach your clinic before any evidence does. In three lessons you will sort them by what the human trials actually show, who paid for those trials, and where each one stands with the regulator.

videoTranscript.en: Most skin peptides reach your clinic before any evidence does. In three lessons you will sort them by what the human trials actually show, who paid for those trials, and where each one stands with the regulator. Start with the molecule. GHK is a three-amino-acid peptide that circulates in human plasma; it was first described in 1973. It binds copper readily, and the copper complex, GHK-Cu, is what skin-care labels mean when they say copper peptide. The proposed mechanism is that GHK-Cu delivers copper to enzymes that build and protect the dermal matrix, such as lysyl oxidase and superoxide dismutase, and shifts gene expression toward wound healing. Two things to hold on to. First, this is a mechanism, which explains why the peptide might work and leaves open whether it does. Second, most of this literature was written by the group that discovered the peptide. Keep both in mind when you reach the trials.

title.en: A plasma tripeptide with a copper habit.

body.en: GHK is a tripeptide found in human plasma, first described in 1973. Bound to copper it becomes GHK-Cu, which is proposed to deliver copper to enzymes such as superoxide dismutase and lysyl oxidase and to switch on wound-healing and antioxidant gene programmes. Most of that mechanistic literature comes from the group that discovered the peptide.

points.en: Endogenous: GHK circulates in human plasma
Proposed: copper delivery to matrix and antioxidant enzymes
Mechanism register only — written largely by the originator

body.en: GHK — glycyl-histidyl-lysine — was isolated from human plasma in 1973. It binds copper readily, and the copper complex is what the skin-care literature calls GHK-Cu.

title.en: What it is proposed to do

body.en: The proposed mechanism is copper delivery to enzymes that build and protect the matrix, plus broad changes in gene expression linked to wound healing.
Much of this work, including the gene-expression reviews, comes from the peptide's discoverer. That does not make it wrong. It does make it a mechanism, and it is worth saying who proposed it.

body.en: A search of PubMed in September 2026 found one randomized controlled trial of topical GHK-Cu in human skin: 2006, healing after CO₂ laser resurfacing. The cosmetic trials cited for anti-ageing claims are manufacturer-sponsored and not indexed. Both Hormonaly guides grade topical use C.

label.en: indexed randomized trial of topical GHK-Cu in human skin

detail.en: Miller et al., 2006 — healing after CO₂ laser resurfacing, not photoageing

means.en: The human evidence for topical GHK-Cu is small: one small indexed trial plus sponsor-run cosmetic studies. GRADE C is the honest ceiling.

doesNot.en: It does not show that GHK-Cu fails, that it treats photoageing, or anything about injecting it. A thin evidence base is an unknown, not a negative.

body.en: Every peptide question has four separate answers. For GHK-Cu they point in different directions, which is exactly why they must not be blended into one sentence.

note.en: Copper delivery to matrix and antioxidant enzymes; gene-expression data from the originator
One small indexed RCT and sponsor-run cosmetic trials; no randomized trials of injection

Category 1 means FDA is still evaluating and does not intend to act against compounders who meet its conditions; an advisory-committee consultation is planned before the end of February 2027. The injectable route has no such standing.

callout.en: A strong mechanism is not a strong trial, and a Category 1 listing is not an approval.

text.en: In the UK, a GHK-Cu serum sold for appearance is a cosmetic, and cosmetics law excludes anything injected (September 2026).

In the EU, copper tripeptide-1 is listed in the Commission's CosIng inventory with a skin-conditioning function (read 25 September 2026). No centrally authorised medicine containing GHK-Cu was found in the Union Register or in EMA's data on authorised, refused and withdrawn medicines (searched 25 September 2026).
In Portugal, no medicine containing GHK-Cu is listed in INFARMED's Infomed register, which includes authorised, lapsed and revoked products (searched 25 September 2026).
In Brazil, ANVISA stated on 2 July 2026 that products presented as peptides called GHK-Cu that promise aesthetic effects or improvement in health conditions are not registered with Anvisa.

In the UAE, the Emirates Drug Establishment (EDE) has held medicines registration since Federal Decree-Law 28/2023, and no registered medical product matching GHK, prezatide, copper tripeptide or copper peptide was found in the EDE register (25 September 2026). In Dubai, the DHA's rules for health facilities prohibit circulating, prescribing, dispensing, administering or using any peptide product unless it is registered or licensed with the EDE (29 July 2026); in Abu Dhabi, the DoH classes topical cosmetic peptides with no systemic effect as low-risk products that stay under existing regulatory pathways, while systemic, regenerative or weakly evidenced peptides face enhanced controls (31 July 2026).

body.en: Topical GHK-Cu is a reasonable cosmetic conversation at GRADE C. Injected GHK-Cu is a different product: no randomized trials, injection-site pain and rash are common because copper irritates tissue, and in the US the injectable route sits outside the Category 1 listing.

points.en: Topical: modest, small-trial support
Injectable: anecdote, common local reactions
Say which route you mean every time

audioScript.en: Here is what that means in the room. Topical GHK-Cu is a reasonable cosmetic conversation, as long as you describe the evidence honestly: small trials, modest effects, grade C. Injected GHK-Cu is not the same product in a stronger form. There are no randomized trials of injection, injection-site pain and rash are common because copper irritates tissue, and in the United States the injectable route sits outside the Category 1 listing that covers non-injectable use. Whatever your role, name the route every time you talk about this peptide.

prescriber.en: In the US, before prescribing a compounded topical, confirm the substance's current 503A status and that the pharmacy is working within it. Do not prescribe GHK-Cu for injection. Record that you discussed a product with small-trial evidence and the patient's reasons for choosing it.

clinical-staff.en: If a patient tells you they inject GHK-Cu, record the product, where it was bought and any site reactions, and bring it to the prescriber. Do not advise on amounts or technique.

advisor.en: Describe topical GHK-Cu products as cosmetics with modest, small-trial support. Anyone injecting a copper peptide should be pointed to a prescriber, not to a better supplier.

text.en: In the UK, anything injected falls outside cosmetics law, and MHRA decides whether it is a medicine from its claims, form and use. In the UK, a GHK-Cu serum presented for appearance is a cosmetic, so there is nothing to prescribe.

In the EU, a substance or mixture intended to be injected is not considered a cosmetic product (Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009, Article 2(2)); the EU borderline manual adds that a product in a vial or ampoule for use by injection cannot be considered a cosmetic product, and should not be marketed with a device that could allow injection or delivery below the epidermis. Whether a product qualifies as a cosmetic is decided case by case by national competent authorities, and the manual says an anti-wrinkle product that significantly restores, corrects or modifies physiological functions by exerting a pharmacological, immunological or metabolic action does not qualify as one (version 5.5, June 2025).

In Portugal, INFARMED states that products administered by injection are not considered cosmetics (as of 25 September 2026), and medicines intended for parenteral administration are subject to medical prescription by law (Estatuto do Medicamento, Art 114(1)(d)).

In Brazil, ANVISA stated on 2 July 2026 that injectable cosmetics do not exist; an injectable product offered as a cosmetic is irregular. Products with 'GHK' in the product name appear as notified cosmetics in ANVISA's public cosmetics data (221 entries, 25 September 2026), and ANVISA cancelled several GHK-Cu cosmetic processes on 29 April 2026 without published reasons (RE 1.771/2026).

In the UAE, the medicines law (Federal Decree-Law 38 of 2024) defines cosmetics as products with a medical effect on the skin, hair or nails, and whether a product requires an Emirates Drug Establishment (EDE) marketing authorisation, and in which category, is determined by an EDE classification letter based on its presentation, composition, use and design. In Dubai, peptide products may be prescribed, dispensed or administered only by licensed, authorised professionals in a licensed health facility (DHA, 29 July 2026); in Abu Dhabi, physicians may prescribe peptide therapies only for clinical indications supported by available scientific evidence, after a documented eligibility assessment and with informed consent that covers benefits, uncertainties, risks, alternatives and the product's regulatory approval status (DoH, 31 July 2026).

title.en: Three families, one question: who ran the trial?

body.en: Signal peptides such as palmitoyl pentapeptide-4 (pal-KTTKS, Matrixyl) are meant to tell fibroblasts to make matrix. SNAP-25 mimics (Argireline and its longer cousin SNAP-8) and Leuphasyl, an enkephalin analogue, are meant to quieten expression lines. Oral collagen peptides are swallowed, not applied. All three families have a trial record, and in all three the question that matters most is who funded it.

points.en: Signal peptides: 'make more matrix'
SNAP-25 mimics: 'relax the line'
Oral collagen: the supplement aisle

blocks.sourceNote: Lupo & Cole 2007 · Lintner & Peschard 2000 · Blanes-Mira 2002 · Errante 2020

body.en: Palmitoylated fragments of matrix proteins, designed to mimic the signals that tell fibroblasts to repair. The palmitoyl tail helps them into the skin.
Argireline copies the end of SNAP-25, a protein botulinum toxin cleaves. SNAP-8 is the maker's eight-residue extension. The premise is a gentler topical version of the same effect.
Hydrolysed collagen taken by mouth, sold as a supplement, with more randomized trials than any topical peptide — and the clearest funding problem.

audioScript.en: Lesson two covers three families that fill the cosmetic and supplement shelves. Signal peptides, like palmitoyl pentapeptide-4, sold as Matrixyl, are fragments of matrix proteins meant to tell fibroblasts to make more collagen. SNAP-25 mimics, Argireline and its longer cousin SNAP-8, copy part of a nerve-terminal protein that botulinum toxin targets; the idea is a gentle, topical version of that effect. And oral collagen peptides are swallowed, not applied. Every one of these has trials behind it. As you go through them, keep asking one question before any other: who ran the trial, and who paid for it.

why.en: GRADE C. A 12-week split-face RCT in 93 women, funded by the manufacturer, and an independent 2023 RCT.
GRADE D. The evidence is the maker's technical dossier; no independent randomized trial was found.

GRADE C in this course. Placebo-controlled RCTs, including an independent head-to-head trial, show modest effects. The two Hormonaly guides disagree (C in Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology, D in the Peptide Pocket Guide); the trials decide it here.
GRADE D. Its efficacy figures come from the manufacturer, and the indexed studies test it mixed with other actives, so none isolates it.
GRADE D. The maker's studies, an in-vitro synergy figure and one small uncontrolled university volunteer study (2014); no independent randomized trial.

body.en: Pooled, oral collagen trials show better hydration, elasticity and wrinkle scores, and the Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology guide grades them C. A 2025 meta-analysis split the same kind of trials by funding and by quality. The benefit appeared only in pharmaceutical-funded and low-quality trials. Unfunded and high-quality trials showed no effect.

label.en: in the 2025 meta-analysis that split oral-collagen trials by funding and quality

means.en: The pooled benefit of oral collagen disappears when you look only at independent or high-quality trials. The course keeps the guide's GRADE C and shows why a downgrade has been proposed to its author.

doesNot.en: It does not show collagen is harmful, and it does not rule out benefit for an individual. It is a statement about the evidence, and it says nothing about topical peptides.

body.en: In the US, cosmetic peptides are cosmetic ingredients, not drugs, and their safety is assessed under a cosmetics framework. Oral collagen is a dietary supplement: it may not claim to treat disease, and product quality and content vary. Neither route has to prove efficacy before sale — which is why the funding question matters.

Dietary supplement: no disease claims; quality varies

audioScript.en: Now the regulatory register, stated for the United States. Cosmetic peptides are cosmetic ingredients, not drugs; their safety is assessed under a cosmetics framework, and nobody has to prove they work before they are sold. Oral collagen is sold as a dietary supplement, so it cannot claim to treat a disease, and what is in the tub varies from brand to brand. That is the whole reason the funding question matters here. When no regulator asks for efficacy, the only efficacy data are the trials someone chose to pay for.

prescriber.en: Nothing here needs a prescription. If you recommend a product, recommend it on evidence, name the grade, and disclose any relationship with the brand. The 'topical Botox' claim is not one to repeat.

clinical-staff.en: When a patient asks which serum 'really works', the accurate answer is modest effects from mostly sponsor-funded trials. Do not describe any of them as an alternative to botulinum toxin.

advisor.en: The claim you can stand behind is modest, small-trial evidence. Supplements cannot be sold as treating a disease; if a patient expects collagen to fix a skin condition, that is a conversation for a prescriber.

text.en: In the UK, a peptide serum is a cosmetic: its responsible person needs a safety assessment and must notify the regulator before sale, and must be able to prove its claims. Oral collagen is a food supplement: no food may claim to prevent, treat or cure disease, and only authorised health claims may be used. In May 2026 the UK advertising regulator ruled a peptide serum's 'clinically proven' lifting claim misleading because the study behind it was small and uncontrolled.

In the EU, a peptide serum sold as a cosmetic needs a responsible person in the EU, a safety assessment with a product safety report and electronic notification to the Commission before it is placed on the market (Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009), and its claims must be supported by adequate and verifiable evidence (Regulation (EU) No 655/2013). Food labelling and advertising may not claim that a food prevents, treats or cures a disease, and health claims on foods are prohibited unless authorised: the Commission refused a claim that a collagen peptide mixture maintains skin health by increasing elasticity and reducing wrinkles, because cause and effect was not established (Regulation (EU) No 1154/2014), and the EU Register lists no authorised claim for collagen itself (searched 25 September 2026).

In Portugal, INFARMED is the competent authority for cosmetics (Decreto-Lei 23/2025), and borderline products must be assessed case by case by the Responsible Person, taking all their characteristics into account (INFARMED, as of 25 September 2026). For food supplement notification, there is no evaluation of the product or validation of labelling; control is carried out afterwards by sampling and may take place at any time (DGAV, as of 25 September 2026).

In Brazil, cosmetic labelling must not contain trade names, brands, images, electronic links or wording that represent therapeutic claims attributed to the use of the product or its ingredients (RDC 907/2024, art. 12). Under ANVISA's January 2025 food supplement guidance, an approved claim is that bioactive hydrolysed collagen peptides with an average molecular weight of 2 kDa help maintain skin health.

In the UAE, the medicines law (Federal Decree-Law 38 of 2024) treats food supplements, oral products that support the diet and do not treat, diagnose or prevent disease, as medical products regulated by the Emirates Drug Establishment (EDE): oral collagen products are registered with the EDE as general-sale-list health products rather than medicines, while ordinary cosmetics need a conformity certificate from the Ministry of Industry and Advanced Technology under Cabinet Resolution 18/2014. Advertising any medical product, social media included, requires EDE approval. In Dubai, the DHA's rules for health facilities ban misleading or unproven peptide claims, such as anti-ageing, cell regeneration or improved appearance, unless the use is within the product's approved status (29 July 2026); in Abu Dhabi, the DoH bars healthcare providers from promoting peptide therapies with misleading or unsubstantiated claims, or advertising them without prior approval from the DoH and relevant authorities (31 July 2026).

body.en: As of September 2026 no randomized efficacy trial of BPC-157 in people has been published in full. FDA's July 2026 briefing found one randomized, placebo-controlled trial reported only as a 2005 meeting abstract: 53 people with ulcerative colitis, two weeks of treatment, and no significant difference from placebo. ClinicalTrials.gov adds a 2015 phase 1 safety study that never posted results, a completed 2025 single-arm product study with no results posted, and a randomized phase 1 trial after rotator-cuff surgery due to start in 2027.

text.en: If you practise in the UK, the route for unlicensed medicines works differently, and lesson 7.2 sets it out.

In the EU, a medicine prepared in a pharmacy on prescription for an individual patient (magistral formula), or to a pharmacopoeia for the pharmacy's own patients (officinal formula), falls outside Directive 2001/83/EC and needs no marketing authorisation under it (Article 3), and each member state may, under its own law, allow an unauthorised medicine for an individual patient on a professional's bona fide unsolicited order, under that professional's direct personal responsibility (Article 5(1)). No centrally authorised medicine containing GHK-Cu, BPC-157 or TB-500 was found in the Union Register or in EMA's data on authorised, refused and withdrawn medicines (searched 25 September 2026).

In Portugal, a magistral formula is a medicine prepared in a community or hospital pharmacy, under a pharmacist's responsibility, on a medical prescription that names the patient, and the prescribing physician must satisfy themselves of its safety and efficacy (Decreto-Lei 95/2004). Compounded medicines may use only raw materials listed in the Portuguese pharmacopoeia, the European pharmacopoeia or another European pharmacopoeia, or in compendial scientific documentation, and one containing any other raw material may not be prescribed.

In Brazil, ANVISA stated on 2 July 2026 that any substance must have passed efficacy and safety assessment before it can be compounded, and that compounding may only be individual, on presentation of a medical prescription, by a compounding pharmacy licensed by local health surveillance. The same notice says BPC-157 and TB-500 are not authorised as food supplements, and that products presented as peptides called GHK-CU, BPC-157, and TB-500 promising aesthetic effects or health improvements are not registered with ANVISA.

In the UAE, the medicines law (Federal Decree-Law 38 of 2024, in force 2 January 2025) exempts medical products compounded in licensed compounding pharmacies from the requirement for a marketing approval from the Emirates Drug Establishment (EDE). In Dubai, the DHA's rules for health facilities prohibit circulating, prescribing, dispensing, administering or using any peptide product unless it is registered or licensed with the EDE (29 July 2026); in Abu Dhabi, the DoH treats peptides as emerging, non-monographed, high-risk substances, and novel substances of unknown risk may be compounded only if monographed, a component of an approved medicine or listed on the DoH's register of compounded substances (compounding standard, August 2026).

text.en: In the EU, a product presented as treating or preventing disease, or used to restore, correct or modify physiological functions by a pharmacological, immunological or metabolic action, is a medicine, and where a product could be both a medicine and another regulated product, medicines law applies (Directive 2001/83/EC, Articles 1(2) and 2(2)). No medicine may be placed on a member state's market without a national or EU-wide marketing authorisation (Article 6(1)), and the directive's exclusion for research concerns medicinal products intended for research and development trials (Article 3(3)).

In Portugal, a medicine is defined as any substance or combination of substances presented as having properties for treating or preventing disease or used in or administered to human beings to restore, correct or modify physiological functions by exerting a pharmacological, immunological or metabolic action, and making, selling, supplying or administering a medicine without the required authorisation is an administrative offence (Estatuto do Medicamento, Arts 3 and 181). No medicine containing GHK-Cu, BPC-157 or TB-500 is listed in INFARMED's Infomed register, which includes authorised, lapsed and revoked products (searched 25 September 2026), and INFARMED does not authorise the import of medicines for personal use (Circular 148/CD, 29 July 2011).

In Brazil, ANVISA stated on 2 July 2026 that products presented as peptides called BPC-157, TB-500 and GHK-Cu are not registered, and that some injectable peptides not regularised in any category (food, medicine, cosmetic or food supplement) are illegal for any health use, including aesthetic use. ANVISA also stated in July 2026 that an investigational medicine is used exclusively in authorised clinical research.

In the UAE, the medicines law (Federal Decree-Law 38 of 2024) has, since 2 January 2025, barred importing, distributing, possessing, selling, using or manufacturing any medical product for circulation without a marketing approval from the Emirates Drug Establishment (EDE), and no registered medical product matching GHK-Cu, BPC-157 or TB-500 was found in the EDE register (25 September 2026). In Dubai, the DHA's rules for health facilities prohibit using any peptide product intended for research use on humans, or for therapeutic purposes, outside a study or clinical trial approved by the competent authority, and bar buying, accepting or using peptide products from websites, social media, individual accounts or unlicensed or unverifiable suppliers (29 July 2026). In Abu Dhabi, the DoH requires compounded peptide formulations to use only certified active ingredients imported under EDE oversight, with peptide products traceable from source to patient (31 July 2026).

objective.en: By the end, you can appraise the neuroendocrinology of the hair follicle and melanocortin receptor system, contrasting FDA-approved therapeutics with the clinical and oncologic hazards of unregulated peptides.

description.en: Lesson 5.1 The hair follicle as an endocrine mini-organ · Lesson 5.2 Afamelanotide, Melanotan II and the melanocortin receptors · Lesson 5.3 Investigational hair peptides, graded.

units.tutorContext: Module 5 teaches the hair follicle and the melanocortin system in four separate registers (mechanism, human evidence, regulatory status, open question). Follicle: ex vivo human scalp follicles run an HPA-like loop (CRH → POMC products → cortisol, with feedback) and a GH/IGF-1-like loop (D, organ culture, Paus group); local DHT miniaturises susceptible follicles (androgenetic alopecia); anagen immune-privilege collapse underlies alopecia areata. Baricitinib: BRAVE-AA1/AA2, 1,200 adults, SALT ≤20 at week 36 in up to 39% on baricitinib vs 3–6% on placebo; FDA-approved 13 Jun 2022 for adults with severe alopecia areata (A). A&RE hair-loss workup: patterned → AGA (topical minoxidil; finasteride in men); diffuse after trigger → telogen effluvium (reassure, ferritin, TSH); patchy smooth ± nail pitting → alopecia areata (dermatology referral, thyroid/autoimmune screen); androgen excess → work-up; ferritin + TSH always; scarring → biopsy; refer severe or rapid AA promptly. Minoxidil (men and women) and finasteride (men): A by RCT meta-analysis (Adil 2017); US: topical minoxidil OTC (approved 1988), finasteride Rx (1997). Melanocortins: skin makes POMC → ACTH, α-MSH, β-endorphin; MC1R pigment, MC2R adrenal, MC3R/MC4R brain (appetite; central sexual effects), MC5R sebum. Afamelanotide: MC1R agonist; two sponsor-funded phase 3 RCTs in EPP (US median 69.4 vs 40.8 pain-free sunlight hours; EU 6.0 vs 0.8); EU authorised 22 Dec 2014 (exceptional circumstances), US 2019; EPP only, manufacturer's implant; US label (Aug 2024) recommends full-body skin examination twice yearly; A for EPP; vitiligo phase 3 has no posted results. Melanotan II: non-selective MC1R/3R/4R/5R agonist, brain-penetrant; only controlled data a 3-man 1996 pilot and a 10-man 1998 ED crossover; guides disagree (Pocket Guide C, A&RE D) — course grades cosmetic use D; case-report harms: darkening/growing and eruptive atypical naevi, melanonychia, ≥5 melanomas all with other risk factors (causation unproven), ischaemic priapism, sympathomimetic toxicity with rhabdomyolysis, PRES; online vials held 43–88% of the label with impurities. Status: approved for no indication; US FDA compounding page (22 Apr 2026) lists it among withdrawn category-2 nominations with safety risks; UK MHRA (17 Apr 2024) injectables are unauthorised medicines, stop immediately; Australia TGA (17 Aug 2026) prescription-only, no ARTG product, not approved for tanning. A&RE: personal or family history of melanoma = absolute contraindication. A patient disclosing use: stop, record product and seller, full skin and nail examination with dermoscopy/baseline photos where available, prompt dermatology referral; never offer afamelanotide as a substitute. PTD-DBM: CXXC5–Dishevelled decoy activating Wnt; one 2017 mouse/tissue study from the developer's group; no human trial published or registered (Sept 2026); D; theoretical off-target Wnt cancer concern untested. Zinc thymulin: zinc-dependent thymic nonapeptide; no indexed human hair study; D. US (14 May 2026): thymulin acetate 503A Category 3; PTD-DBM on no list; neither on the bulks list (21 CFR 216.23). UK (checked 25 Sep 2026): baricitinib licensed for severe AA (NICE TA926 not recommended, Oct 2023); men's minoxidil foam on the General Sales List; finasteride for hair loss private prescription only, MHRA strengthened depression/suicidality/sexual-dysfunction warnings 11 May 2026 (patient card; ask about depression); afamelanotide licensed under exceptional circumstances, specialist porphyria centres, NICE HST27 not recommended (Jul 2023); Melanotan II an unauthorised medicine (MHRA FOI 24/274); a peptide spray made for one patient = unlicensed special, behind any licensed option (MHRA GN14). Never give doses, regimens, reconstitution, sourcing or administration advice; adapt the 'what you do next' to the learner's role (prescriber, clinical staff, advisor) without changing grades or regulatory facts. No CME credit is currently offered.

In three lessons you will see how the follicle and the pigment system run on the skin's own hormones, why one melanocortin drug is approved while its gray-market cousin is approved nowhere, and how to grade the hair peptides patients bring to you.

videoTranscript.en: Two requests reach aesthetic clinics well ahead of their evidence: a peptide to regrow hair and an injection to tan. In three lessons you will see how the follicle and the pigment system run on the skin's own hormones, why one melanocortin drug is approved while its gray-market cousin is approved nowhere, and how to grade the hair peptides patients bring to you. Each hair follicle behaves like a small gland. When researchers keep human scalp follicles alive in culture, the follicles answer corticotropin-releasing hormone the way the pituitary and adrenal glands do. They make ACTH and alpha-MSH, they secrete cortisol, and cortisol-like signals feed back to switch the stimulus down. On the scalp, an enzyme called five-alpha-reductase turns testosterone into dihydrotestosterone, and in genetically susceptible follicles that hormone drives the gradual shrinking behind pattern hair loss. Most of this biology comes from tissue kept alive outside the body, so hold it as mechanism, a reason something might matter in patients.

title.en: A follicle that runs its own hormones.

body.en: Human scalp hair follicles kept alive in the laboratory answer corticotropin-releasing hormone by making ACTH and α-MSH and secreting cortisol, with a feedback loop like the adrenal axis. They also run a growth hormone and IGF-1 loop of their own. Locally made dihydrotestosterone shrinks genetically susceptible scalp follicles, the process behind pattern hair loss. Growing follicles are shielded from immune attack, and alopecia areata begins when that shield fails.

points.en: Local stress axis: CRH → ACTH → cortisol, with feedback
Local androgen switch: testosterone → DHT in the scalp
Immune privilege: its collapse drives alopecia areata

blocks.sourceNote: Ito 2005 · Horesh 2023 · Bertolini 2020 · Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology, ch. 6

body.en: Organ-cultured human scalp follicles respond to CRH by making POMC products and secreting cortisol, and hydrocortisone in turn damps follicular CRH, the adrenal axis in miniature.

title.en: Its own growth and androgen signals

body.en: Outside the body, follicles also run a GH and IGF-1 loop. In susceptible scalp follicles, locally made DHT drives the miniaturisation of pattern hair loss.
Growing follicles show little antigen to immune cells. When that privilege collapses, T cells and natural killer cells attack the bulb and alopecia areata follows.

audioScript.en: Each hair follicle behaves like a small gland. When researchers keep human scalp follicles alive in culture, the follicles answer corticotropin-releasing hormone the way the pituitary and adrenal glands do. They make ACTH and alpha-MSH, they secrete cortisol, and cortisol-like signals feed back to switch the stimulus down. The same follicles run a growth hormone and IGF-1 loop of their own. On the scalp, an enzyme called five-alpha-reductase turns testosterone into dihydrotestosterone, and in genetically susceptible follicles that hormone drives the gradual shrinking behind pattern hair loss. Growing follicles also hide from the immune system. When that protection collapses, immune cells attack the hair bulb, and the result is alopecia areata. Most of this biology comes from tissue kept alive outside the body, so hold it as mechanism, a reason something might matter in patients.

body.en: When immune privilege fails, the attack depends on cytokine signals that JAK inhibitors interrupt. Two randomized phase 3 trials tested oral baricitinib in 1,200 adults with severe alopecia areata. In the US, FDA approved baricitinib for adults with severe alopecia areata on 13 June 2022. The Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology guide grades it A.

blocks.sourceNote: King 2022 (BRAVE-AA1 and -AA2) · FDA approval letter, 13 Jun 2022

label.en: adults with severe alopecia areata in the two phase 3 trials of baricitinib (2022)

detail.en: At 36 weeks, up to 39% of patients on baricitinib had at least 80% of their scalp hair, against 3–6% on placebo

means.en: Interrupting the immune signalling behind collapsed privilege regrows hair in severe alopecia areata. That is approval-grade evidence (A), and it shows what real follicle evidence looks like.

doesNot.en: It says nothing about pattern hair loss, cosmetic thinning or any peptide. Both trials were funded by the manufacturer, and the authors called for longer trials.

text.en: In the UK, baricitinib is licensed for severe alopecia areata in adults, and NICE did not recommend it for NHS use in October 2023, on cost-effectiveness.

In the EU, baricitinib (Olumiant) has been centrally authorised since 13 February 2017; its indications include severe alopecia areata in adults and adolescents aged 12 and over, and it is prescription-only, started by a doctor experienced in the condition (EMA). Since EMA's January 2023 review, JAK inhibitors including Olumiant should be used in people aged 65 or over, at raised cardiovascular or cancer risk, or long-term smokers only if no suitable alternative exists, and this applies to alopecia areata.
In Portugal, Olumiant (baricitinib) is classified as a restricted-prescription medicine (MSRM restrita - Alínea a), according to INFARMED's Infomed register on 25 September 2026.

In Brazil, baricitinib (Olumiant) has been registered by ANVISA since 26 November 2018, and its current label includes severe alopecia areata in adults and adolescents aged 12 or over weighing at least 30 kg (checked 25 September 2026).

In the UAE, the Emirates Drug Establishment (EDE) has held medicines registration since Federal Decree-Law 28/2023, and the medicines law is Federal Decree-Law 38 of 2024. The EDE register lists Olumiant (baricitinib) tablets, registered since 8 June 2017, as Prescription Only and files them under rheumatic diseases; it does not show whether alopecia areata is an approved UAE indication (25 September 2026).

body.en: The Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology guide's first-pass hair-loss workup asks four questions in order. Each yes points to a different condition and a different next step.

note.en: Topical minoxidil; finasteride in men; treat coexisting iron or thyroid problems

label.en: Diffuse shedding after a trigger? (illness, delivery, diet, a drug)

note.en: Remove the trigger, reassure, recheck ferritin and TSH

label.en: Patchy, smooth loss? (with or without nail pitting)

note.en: Dermatology referral; screen for thyroid and autoimmune disease

label.en: Signs of androgen excess? (hirsutism, acne, irregular periods)

note.en: Follow the guide's acne and androgen pathway
Add androgens if there are virilising signs; a scarring pattern needs a biopsy

title.en: Work up the hair loss before anyone mentions a peptide.

body.en: Pattern, trigger, patches and androgens decide the treatment. Pooled randomized trials support topical minoxidil in men and women and finasteride in men. In the US, as of September 2026, topical minoxidil is FDA-approved and sold over the counter, finasteride for pattern hair loss is a prescription drug, and baricitinib is approved for adults with severe alopecia areata.

points.en: Workup first: ferritin and TSH in everyone
Approved options exist, with A-grade evidence
Severe or fast-spreading alopecia areata goes to dermatology

body.en: Pattern, trigger, patches and signs of androgen excess sort most hair loss. Ferritin and TSH are checked in everyone, and a scarring pattern goes to biopsy.
Topical minoxidil in men and women and finasteride in men have pooled randomized-trial support (A). In the US minoxidil is sold over the counter and finasteride needs a prescription.
Severe or fast-spreading alopecia areata goes to dermatology, where a JAK inhibitor is an approved option for adults.

audioScript.en: Most requests for a hair peptide skip the diagnosis. Start with the pattern, ask about a trigger, look for patches and nail pitting, and look for signs of androgen excess. Check ferritin and thyroid function every time, and send a scarring pattern for biopsy. The approved options already carry strong evidence. Pooled randomized trials support topical minoxidil in men and women and finasteride in men. In the United States minoxidil is sold over the counter, while finasteride for hair loss needs a prescription. Severe or fast-spreading alopecia areata belongs with a dermatologist, where a JAK inhibitor is an approved option for adults. Whatever your role, the workup comes before the product.

prescriber.en: Complete the workup and record the pattern before prescribing. Offer the approved options with their grades, refer severe or rapidly progressive alopecia areata, and document any investigational product the patient raises and what you advised. In the UK, before prescribing finasteride, ask about any history of depression, give the patient card, and review mood and sexual side effects.

clinical-staff.en: Note the pattern, the timeline and any recent trigger, photograph the scalp with consent if your setting allows, and pass it to the prescriber. Patchy or fast-spreading loss needs prompt escalation.

advisor.en: Explain what the approved options are and what their evidence shows. A patient with new, patchy, scarring or fast-spreading hair loss needs a prescriber before any product.

text.en: In the UK, topical minoxidil is licensed and a men's foam is on general sale, finasteride for hair loss is available only on private prescription, and baricitinib is licensed for severe alopecia areata in adults. In May 2026 MHRA strengthened its warnings that finasteride is associated with depression, suicidal thoughts and sexual dysfunction that may persist after stopping.

In the EU, topical minoxidil is authorised nationally, finasteride tablets and a finasteride skin spray are authorised in various member states for early androgenetic alopecia in men aged 18 to 41 (EMA, 2025), and baricitinib (Olumiant) is centrally authorised and prescription-only, with severe alopecia areata in adults and adolescents aged 12 and over among its indications. After an EU-wide review endorsed on 19 June 2025, suicidal ideation is a confirmed side effect of finasteride tablets, and packs of the hair-loss tablets carry a patient card.

In Portugal, topical minoxidil is a non-prescription medicine (MNSRM), and the label of Minox 5 solution covers alopecia areata as well as androgenetic alopecia in men and women. Finasteride for hair loss (Propecia) is prescription-only (MSRM), and baricitinib (Olumiant) is a restricted-prescription medicine (MSRM restrita – point a) (INFARMED's Infomed register, 25 September 2026).

In Brazil, minoxidil products such as Aloxidil are indicated for androgenetic alopecia in adult men, and finasteride products such as Pro Hair are indicated for the treatment of men with male-pattern baldness (androgenetic alopecia). Baricitinib (Olumiant) is indicated for adult and adolescent patients aged 12 years or older and weighing at least 30 kg with severe alopecia areata (ANVISA, 25 September 2026).

In the UAE, the Emirates Drug Establishment (EDE) has held medicines registration since Federal Decree-Law 28/2023, and the medicines law is Federal Decree-Law 38 of 2024. The EDE register lists topical minoxidil (for example Regaine solution, a Pharmacist Only Medicine), oral finasteride (Propecia, Prescription Only), a topical finasteride spray registered in March 2025 (Fincrezo, Prescription Only) and Olumiant (baricitinib, Prescription Only), without showing whether alopecia areata is an approved UAE indication (25 September 2026).

prompt.en: A 32-year-old woman asks for a compounded peptide scalp spray. Diffuse shedding began three months after she gave birth; there are no patches and no signs of androgen excess. What comes first?

text.en: Start the spray now, since peptides act on the follicle directly.

why.en: That skips the diagnosis. The pattern points to telogen effluvium, and peptide sprays such as PTD-DBM or zinc thymulin have no human trial behind them.

text.en: Treat it as likely telogen effluvium: reassure, check ferritin and TSH, and reassess the pattern before any product.

why.en: Correct. Diffuse shedding after a trigger is the guide's telogen-effluvium branch, and ferritin and TSH are checked in everyone.

text.en: Refer her for a JAK inhibitor.

why.en: JAK inhibitors are for severe alopecia areata, which shows as patchy, smooth loss. This pattern is different.

feedback.en: Diagnose the pattern first; the product question comes after.

title.en: Five receptors, one family of hormones.

body.en: Skin makes proopiomelanocortin (POMC) and cuts it into ACTH, α-MSH and β-endorphin, and the same cells carry the receptors that answer them. Those peptides act on five melanocortin receptors. MC1R drives pigment in skin and hair, MC2R answers ACTH in the adrenal gland, MC3R and MC4R act in the brain on appetite, and MC5R governs sebum. Which receptors a drug reaches decides what else it does.

points.en: MC1R: pigment of skin and hair
MC2R: adrenal · MC5R: sebum
MC3R and MC4R: appetite, in the brain

blocks.sourceNote: Slominski & Wortsman 2000 · Laiho & Murray 2022 · Böhm 2025

body.en: Skin cells make POMC and cut it into ACTH, α-MSH and β-endorphin, and they carry the receptors that answer them.
MC1R pigment, MC2R adrenal, MC3R and MC4R appetite in the brain, MC5R sebum. Reviewers note the real distribution is probably wider than this tidy map.
A drug that stays on MC1R mostly changes pigment. A drug that reaches the brain's receptors brings nausea, appetite loss and erections with it.

audioScript.en: Pigment starts with hormones the skin makes for itself. Skin cells produce a precursor called POMC and cut it into ACTH, alpha-MSH and beta-endorphin, and the same cells carry the receptors that answer them. There are five melanocortin receptors. MC1R sets the pigment of skin and hair. MC2R is the adrenal receptor for ACTH. MC3R and MC4R work in the brain on appetite, and central receptors also drive sexual responses. MC5R governs sebum. Researchers caution that the real map is messier, with receptors turning up in more tissues than the textbook suggests. For this lesson one idea matters most. A drug that stays on MC1R mostly changes pigment, and a drug that reaches the brain's receptors brings other effects with it.
