title.en: One receptor family, two very different molecules.

body.en: Afamelanotide and Melanotan II are both synthetic relatives of α-MSH. Compare them register by register and the resemblance ends at the receptor.

blocks.sourceNote: Langendonk 2015 · EMA Scenesse EPAR · FDA Scenesse label (Aug 2024) · Dorr 1996 · Wessells 1998 · Böhm 2025

value.en: Afamelanotide: MC1R agonist · Melanotan II: non-selective

note.en: Melanotan II also acts on MC3R, MC4R and MC5R and reaches the brain

value.en: Afamelanotide: A, for EPP only · Melanotan II: D

note.en: Two phase 3 trials in erythropoietic protoporphyria, against a three-volunteer pilot and a ten-man erectile-dysfunction study from the 1990s. The Peptide Pocket Guide rates Melanotan II C and the Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology guide D; with no trial of tanning, this course uses D.

value.en: Afamelanotide: EU 2014, US 2019 · Melanotan II: none

note.en: Afamelanotide is approved only for EPP, as the manufacturer's implant. Melanotan II is approved for no indication anywhere.
A phase 3 trial of afamelanotide in vitiligo began in 2023 and has posted no results. Whether Melanotan II causes melanoma is unproven.

callout.en: A shared receptor does not bring a shared approval.

text.en: In the UK, afamelanotide is licensed under exceptional circumstances and prescribed only in specialist porphyria centres, and NICE did not recommend it for NHS use (July 2023).

In the EU, afamelanotide (Scenesse implant) is authorised for erythropoietic protoporphyria, under exceptional circumstances (European Commission, 22 December 2014), and is prescribed only by specialists in recognised EPP centres.

In Portugal, Scenesse is authorised through the EU procedure but classified as a restricted-prescription medicine for exclusive hospital use (MSRM restrita, alínea a), and no presentation is marketed in Portugal (INFARMED's Infomed register, 25 September 2026).

In Brazil, no registered medicine containing afamelanotide (Scenesse) was found: ANVISA's open-data register and its online medicines search returned no match on 25 September 2026, and the substance is absent from ANVISA's substance dictionary.

In the UAE, the Emirates Drug Establishment (EDE) has held medicines registration since Federal Decree-Law 28/2023, and the medicines law is Federal Decree-Law 38 of 2024. An ingredient and product-name search of the EDE register found no registered product containing afamelanotide, and none named Scenesse (25 September 2026).

body.en: Erythropoietic protoporphyria (EPP) is a rare disorder in which sunlight causes acute, severe pain. In the US phase 3 trial, adults on afamelanotide spent a median 69.4 hours in direct sunlight without pain over six months, against 40.8 hours on placebo. The European trial also showed more pain-free time and fewer phototoxic reactions. Both trials were funded by the manufacturer.

blocks.sourceNote: Langendonk 2015 (NEJM) · FDA Scenesse label, Aug 2024 · EMA EPAR

label.en: median pain-free hours in direct sunlight over six months, afamelanotide vs placebo (US phase 3 trial, 94 adults with EPP)

detail.en: Langendonk et al., NEJM 2015 · European trial, 74 adults: 6.0 vs 0.8 hours over nine months

means.en: Afamelanotide lets people with EPP spend more time in sunlight without pain. That is approval-grade evidence (A) for one rare disease.

doesNot.en: It says nothing about cosmetic tanning, about Melanotan II, or about unsupervised injections. Even in EPP, the US label recommends a full-body skin examination twice a year.

body.en: The harms of Melanotan II come from case reports and reviews, so they show what can happen without telling you how often. Reported skin effects include darkening and growth of existing moles, crops of new and sometimes atypical naevi, and dark bands in the nails. At least five melanomas have been reported during or after use, each in someone with other risk factors, so causation is unproven. Systemic reports include ischaemic priapism needing surgery and a stimulant-like toxic reaction with rhabdomyolysis, and FDA lists posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome among published serious events.

points.en: Skin: changing moles, eruptive naevi, melanonychia
Melanoma: reported, causation unproven
Systemic: priapism, rhabdomyolysis, encephalopathy

blocks.sourceNote: Habbema 2017 · Cardones 2009 · Paurobally 2013 · Hjuler 2014 · Mallory 2021 · Nelson 2012 · FDA compounding safety page

body.en: Existing moles darken and grow, new naevi appear in crops, some atypical on histology, and nails can develop dark bands. In one report the new naevi faded after the injections stopped.
At least five melanomas have been reported during or after use. Every patient had other risk factors, such as fair skin, sunbed use or a family history.
Nausea, flushing and yawning are common. Reported emergencies include ischaemic priapism needing surgery, rhabdomyolysis with kidney injury, and encephalopathy.

audioScript.en: Now the harms, and the kind of evidence behind them. Everything here comes from case reports and reviews, which tell you what can happen and leave open how often it does. In the skin, existing moles darken and grow, new moles erupt in crops, some of them atypical under the microscope, and dark bands can appear in the nails. At least five melanomas have been reported during or after Melanotan use. Each patient had other risk factors, such as fair skin, sunbed use or a family history, so causation is unproven, and the concern rests on a drug that pushes melanocytes to multiply. Beyond the skin, reports describe priapism that needed surgery, a stimulant-like toxic reaction with muscle breakdown and kidney injury, and a brain swelling syndrome that FDA lists among the published serious events.

Under Law 6.360/1976, no product covered by the law, including an imported one, may be manufactured, offered for sale or supplied for consumption before being registered with the Ministry of Health.

In the UAE, the Emirates Drug Establishment (EDE) has held medicines registration since Federal Decree-Law 28/2023, and the medicines law is Federal Decree-Law 38 of 2024; no melanotan product was found in the EDE register (25 September 2026). In Abu Dhabi, the Department of Health (Circular 112/2025, 2 July 2025), relaying an EDE warning on Melanotan II ('Barbie drug'), requires facilities to prohibit its importation, distribution, marketing or use. text.en: They are different molecules. Afamelanotide is approved only for erythropoietic protoporphyria; Melanotan II acts on several receptors, is approved nowhere, and is linked in case reports to changing moles and priapism.

title.en: A Wnt switch and a zinc question.

body.en: PTD-DBM joins a cell-penetrating peptide to a short decoy sequence that stops the protein CXXC5 from binding Dishevelled. Freed from that brake, Wnt/β-catenin signalling rises, and in mice hair regrew faster. Its developers also found CXXC5 raised in human balding scalp. Zinc thymulin is a thymic peptide that is active only when bound to zinc. How it might act on hair has never been defined, and whether any effect would come from the peptide or the zinc is unknown.

points.en: PTD-DBM: releases a Wnt brake (mouse data)
Zinc thymulin: a zinc-dependent thymic peptide
Both: mechanism first, human data absent

blocks.sourceNote: Lee 2017 (J Invest Dermatol) · Dardenne 1982 · Peptide Pocket Guide

body.en: A cell-penetrating tag carries a decoy sequence into follicle cells. The decoy keeps CXXC5 off Dishevelled, so Wnt signalling can rise.
Faster hair regrowth, and new follicles in healed wounds, in mice. The work came from the developer's own group, which also found CXXC5 raised in human balding scalp tissue.
A thymic hormone that works only with zinc bound. Its proposed hair effect has no defined mechanism and no indexed human study.

audioScript.en: Two peptides are sold for hair, and both arrive with better stories than data. PTD-DBM joins a cell-penetrating fragment borrowed from an HIV protein to a short decoy sequence. Inside follicle cells, the decoy keeps a protein called CXXC5 from binding its partner, Dishevelled, and that releases a brake on Wnt signalling, a pathway involved in hair regrowth. In mice, hair regrew faster and follicles formed in healed wounds. The work came from the developer's own group. Zinc thymulin is a thymic hormone that becomes active only when zinc binds to it. How it might help hair has never been defined, and nobody has shown whether any effect would come from the peptide or from the zinc. Hold both as mechanism, and look for the human trial.

audioScript.en: Stated for the United States, the regulatory picture is short. On FDA's category lists of the fourteenth of May, twenty twenty-six, thymulin acetate sits in Category 3, meaning it was nominated without enough information for FDA to evaluate, and it falls outside the enforcement discretion that Category 1 substances receive. PTD-DBM appears on none of the three lists. Neither substance is on the 503A bulks list itself. The evidence grade for both is D. So when a patient asks for a compounded hair spray, give the grade plainly, go back to the diagnosis, and describe the approved options and what they can offer.

prescriber.en: Check a substance's current 503A status before any compounding conversation; neither peptide has Category 1 standing today. If a patient already uses one, record the product, the source and the grade you quoted, and offer the workup and the approved options. In the UK, a special needs a clinical need that the licensed options cannot meet; cost and convenience do not count.

text.en: In the UK, a spray made up for one patient would be an unlicensed 'special', and MHRA guidance says an unlicensed product should not be used where a UK-licensed one, such as minoxidil, could meet the patient's need.

In the EU, a medicine prepared in a pharmacy for an individual patient on prescription (a magistral formula) falls outside Directive 2001/83/EC (Article 3). A search of the Union Register and EMA's medicines data found no centrally authorised medicine containing thymulin or PTD-DBM (25 September 2026).

In Portugal, a magistral formula may use only raw materials listed in the Portuguese or European pharmacopoeia, another European pharmacopoeia or compendial scientific documentation, and the prescribing physician must satisfy themselves of its safety and efficacy (Decreto-Lei 95/2004). INFARMED's Infomed register lists no medicine containing thymulin or PTD-DBM (25 September 2026).

In Brazil, ANVISA stated on 2 July 2026 that a substance must have passed efficacy and safety assessment before it can be compounded, and that compounding may only be individual, on prescription, by a pharmacy licensed by local health surveillance. A search of ANVISA's register found no registered medicine containing PTD-DBM or thymulin (25 September 2026), though immunomodulators such as thymomodulin are registered.

In the UAE, the Emirates Drug Establishment (EDE) has held medicines registration since Federal Decree-Law 28/2023; under the medicines law, Federal Decree-Law 38 of 2024, products compounded in licensed compounding pharmacies need no marketing approval, and no product containing thymulin or PTD-DBM was found in the EDE register (25 September 2026). In Dubai, the Dubai Health Authority (DHA) prohibits circulating, prescribing, dispensing or using any peptide product that is not registered or licensed with the EDE (29 July 2026). In Abu Dhabi, the Department of Health (DoH) lets compounded peptide formulations use only certified active ingredients imported under EDE oversight (31 July 2026), and its August 2026 compounding standard treats peptides as emerging, high-risk substances that may be compounded only if monographed, part of an approved medicine or listed on the DoH's register of compounded substances.

title.en: The growth-hormone axis and the skin

description.en: Lesson 6.1 Growth hormone and IGF-1 in the skin · Lesson 6.2 GHRH analogues and secretagogues: what stands behind each · Lesson 6.3 Signs of excess, oedema and mitogenic risk.

units.tutorContext: Module 6 teaches the growth-hormone/IGF-1 axis in four separate registers (mechanism, human evidence, regulatory status, open question). Mechanism: GH receptor mainly on dermal fibroblasts (collagen, fibroblast growth); IGF-1 made by fibroblasts/melanocytes acts on keratinocyte IGF-1R (proliferation); hair follicles run a local GHRH-GH-IGF-1 loop ex vivo (all D). Somatopause: GH/IGF-1 fall with age; read IGF-1 against age/sex ranges. Human skin evidence: GHD = thinner epidermis, less sweating (Lange 2001, C); acromegaly = GAG deposition and oedema; GH speeds donor-site/burn healing in >40% TBSA burns (Cochrane 2014, 13 small RCTs, C, more hyperglycaemia); Rudman 1990 skin +7.1% P=0.07, n=12, no placebo (D). Healthy older adults: GH gives ~2 kg less fat/2 kg more lean, more oedema, arthralgia, carpal tunnel, diabetes trend (Liu 2007, B; A&RE says A); US: knowingly distributing GH for anti-ageing is a federal offence (21 USC 333(e)). Tesamorelin: two phase 3 RCTs (806 pooled), VAT about -15% vs placebo; FDA-approved 2010 for excess abdominal fat in HIV lipodystrophy only; GRADE A for that indication only; label: IGF-1 >2 SDS in 47%, diabetes-range HbA1c 5% vs 1%, effects of prolonged IGF-1 elevation unknown. No RCT with a skin outcome for tesamorelin, CJC-1295, ipamorelin or IGF-1 LR3 (PubMed Sept 2026); Khorram 1997 GHRH(1-29) analogue, n=19, caliper skin thickness (D). CJC-1295 with DAC: phase 1 hormone levels only (D; guides say C); CJC-1295 without DAC and IGF-1 LR3: no human studies (D); ipamorelin: phase 2 ileus RCT negative (D for anti-ageing); sermorelin adult use D; ibutamoren (MK-677): IGF-1 and lean mass up, no function gain, glucose worse, hip-fracture trial stopped for heart failure. US status (FDA lists 22 Apr and 14 May 2026): no GH-axis peptide on the 503A bulks list (21 CFR 216.23); ibutamoren 503A+503B Category 2; GHRP-2/-6 503A Category 3; CJC-1295 and ipamorelin 503A nominations withdrawn (ipamorelin 503B Category 2); PCAC Oct 2024 voted against ipamorelin (0-12-1) and ibutamoren (1-13); sermorelin: no marketed approved product (Geref withdrawn 2009, not for safety), in no 503A category. GH excess signs: puffy thick face/hands/feet, oily skin, hyperhidrosis, skin tags, acanthosis, acral/jaw growth; on drugs: oedema, arthralgia, paraesthesia, carpal tunnel; somatropin label: watch nevi. Endocrine Society: measure IGF-1 for acral/facial features; suggest when sleep apnoea, T2D, arthritis, carpal tunnel, hyperhidrosis, hypertension cluster. Route to prescriber/endocrinology. Cancer: mechanism plausible; observational IGF-1 associations modest (Renehan 2004 B, UK Biobank C); acromegaly SIR 1.5 pooled vs 1.1 nationwide; GH replacement cohorts reassuring (SAGhE, 2022 consensus); secretagogue/LR3 long-term data absent. UK (checked 25 Sep 2026): somatropin is a prescription-only medicine (licensed for GHD and specific growth disorders) and a Class C controlled drug (Misuse of Drugs Act 1971); MHRA's products database holds no product information for tesamorelin, sermorelin or ipamorelin, so any would be unlicensed; unlicensed 'specials' only for an individual patient's special need (MHRA GN14). Never give doses, cycles, stacks, reconstitution, sourcing or IGF-1 targets; adapt only the 'what you do next' to role (prescriber, clinical staff, advisor). No CME credit is currently offered.

learningObjectives.en: Examine the cellular pathways by which GH and IGF-1 regulate keratinocyte proliferation, dermal fibroblast activity, and extracellular matrix composition.
Differentiate validated clinical trial indications of somatropin, sermorelin, and tesamorelin from off-label claims regarding unapproved secretagogues (CJC-1295, ipamorelin).
Identify dermatologic and systemic red-flag signs of excessive somatotropic stimulation, including mucopolysaccharide deposition, peripheral edema, and theoretical neoplastic risks.

videoTranscript.en: Growth hormone and IGF-1 genuinely shape skin, and one peptide on this axis has approval-grade trials. Most of what patients are offered has much less behind it. In three lessons you will separate the physiology from the promise, the approved from the anecdotal, and the side-effects you can see from the risks nobody has measured. Two layers of skin listen to two different parts of the same axis. Growth hormone speaks mainly to the dermis. Its receptor is expressed more on fibroblasts than on keratinocytes, and in culture growth hormone increases fibroblast numbers and supports collagen synthesis, sometimes directly and sometimes through IGF-1. The epidermis listens to IGF-1. Keratinocytes carry the IGF-1 receptor, their neighbours in the dermis supply the hormone, and in culture IGF-1 makes keratinocytes divide where growth hormone on its own does nothing. With age, growth-hormone pulses and IGF-1 fall steadily, a change called the somatopause. Hold all of this as mechanism. It explains why the axis could matter for skin. Whether changing it helps a patient is a separate question, and the trials answer it.

title.en: Two hormones, two layers of skin.

body.en: Growth hormone acts mostly in the dermis. Its receptor is expressed more by fibroblasts than by keratinocytes, and it increases fibroblast numbers and supports collagen synthesis. IGF-1, made locally by fibroblasts and melanocytes, reaches keratinocytes through the IGF-1 receptor and makes them divide. Human hair follicles even run their own small growth-hormone loop in the laboratory. With age, GH secretion and IGF-1 fall steadily; this is the somatopause.

points.en: GH: dermal fibroblasts and collagen
IGF-1: keratinocyte proliferation, supplied locally
Somatopause: GH and IGF-1 fall with age

blocks.sourceNote: Tavakkol 1992 · Edmondson 2003 · Horesh 2023 · Veldhuis 2008 · Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology, ch. 2 and 6

body.en: Growth-hormone receptors sit mainly on dermal fibroblasts. GH, directly or through IGF-1, supports fibroblast growth and collagen synthesis.
Keratinocytes carry the IGF-1 receptor but make little IGF-1 themselves; fibroblasts supply it. In culture, IGF-1 makes keratinocytes divide and GH on its own does not.
GH pulses and IGF-1 fall from early adulthood. Reference ranges are age-adjusted, so an IGF-1 that is low for a 25-year-old is often normal for the patient's age.

title.en: A much-cited skin result, read again.

body.en: In 1990 a much-cited New England Journal of Medicine study gave growth hormone for six months to 12 healthy men over 60, with nine untreated men for comparison and no placebo. Lean mass rose and fat fell. Skin thickness rose 7.1%, with P = 0.07, short of statistical significance. A small 1996 randomized trial in 28 older men found 15% more collagen laid down in implanted wound tubes on GH, a laboratory surrogate for repair.

blocks.sourceNote: Rudman 1990 · Papadakis 1996

label.en: rise in skin thickness in 12 older men given growth hormone for six months (1990)

detail.en: P = 0.07 · nine untreated men as comparison · no placebo

means.en: A skin result still quoted for growth hormone comes from 12 treated men, without a placebo, and it missed statistical significance. Graded on its design, it is D.

doesNot.en: It does not show that GH thins skin or that it fails in true deficiency, and it says nothing about secretagogues. It shows how thin the direct skin evidence for growth hormone in healthy ageing is.

title.en: Mechanism, human evidence or open question?

body.en: Six things you will hear about growth hormone and skin, each accurate as worded. Before you see the answer, decide what kind of statement each one is.

blocks.sourceNote: Tavakkol 1992 · Lange 2001 · Breederveld 2014 (Cochrane) · Horesh 2023 · Ben-Shlomo & Melmed 2006

value.en: IGF-1 makes them divide in culture; GH alone does not
Adults with untreated deficiency have a thinner epidermis on biopsy
GH shortened donor-site healing by about three days in adults
Follicles keep a GH–IGF-1 loop running outside the body
Glycosaminoglycan deposits and oedema thicken and puff the skin
Whether raising GH or IGF-1 makes facial skin look younger

callout.en: Knowing what growth hormone does to skin in disease is different from knowing what it does to healthy skin.

prompt.en: Tap the kind of statement each one is.

label.en: IGF-1 makes keratinocytes divide in culture; GH alone does not

why.en: Mechanism (D). Cell-culture work from 1992 explains a pathway; it tells you nothing about a patient's skin.

label.en: Adults with untreated GH deficiency have a thinner epidermis on biopsy

why.en: Human evidence (C), small and observational: 45 people biopsied in 2001. Treatment of childhood-onset deficiency did not fully normalise the skin.

label.en: GH shortened donor-site healing in adults with major burns

why.en: Human evidence (C): 13 small randomized trials pooled by Cochrane in 2014, with more hyperglycaemia on GH and a risk of bias. Burns over 40% of the body, far from cosmetic use.

label.en: Hair follicles keep a GH–IGF-1 loop running outside the body

why.en: Mechanism (D). An ex vivo finding from 2023 about follicle biology.

label.en: In acromegaly, glycosaminoglycan deposits and oedema thicken the skin

why.en: Human evidence from disease. It shows what too much growth hormone does to skin, and says nothing about a cosmetic benefit.

label.en: Whether raising GH or IGF-1 makes a healthy adult's facial skin look younger

why.en: Open question. No randomized trial has measured it, and the 1990 skin result missed statistical significance.

done.en: Six sorted. Two are mechanism, three are human evidence, and the one patients ask about is still an open question.

title.en: Deficiency is a diagnosis. Decline is ageing.

body.en: In healthy older adults, randomized trials of growth hormone show small shifts in body composition, about 2 kg less fat and 2 kg more lean mass, with more oedema, joint pain, carpal tunnel syndrome and a trend towards diabetes. Strength and endurance change little. The Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology guide grades its advice against treatment A; graded on the trials themselves the evidence is B, and the conclusion is the same. In the US, as of September 2026, knowingly distributing growth hormone for anti-ageing is a federal offence.

points.en: Healthy ageing: small body-composition change, more side-effects
Grade B on the trials (guide: A), same conclusion
US: anti-ageing distribution is a federal offence

blocks.sourceNote: Liu 2007 · Blackman 2002 · 21 U.S.C. 333(e) · Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology, ch. 14 · Genotropin UK SmPC · Misuse of Drugs Act 1971, Sch. 2

body.en: Pooled randomized trials in healthy older adults: about 2 kg less fat, 2 kg more lean mass, weight unchanged.
More soft-tissue oedema, joint pain, carpal tunnel syndrome and gynaecomastia, and a trend towards diabetes. In one trial, 39% of women on GH developed oedema, against none on placebo.
Growth hormone is for diagnosed deficiency and a short list of approved conditions. In the US, distributing it for anti-ageing is a federal offence.

audioScript.en: Here the physiology meets the waiting room. A patient in their fifties has read that growth hormone falls with age and asks whether topping it up would help their skin. The trials in healthy older adults answer that. Pooled, they show about two kilograms less fat and two kilograms more lean mass, with more swelling, joint pain, carpal tunnel symptoms and a drift towards diabetes, while strength and stamina change little. Graded on those trials the evidence is B, consistent and independent though small, and the Aesthetic and Regenerative Endocrinology guide gives its advice against treatment an A. Both land in the same place. Growth hormone treats a diagnosed deficiency and a short list of approved conditions. In the United States, distributing it for anti-ageing is a federal offence. Whatever your role, name the decline for what it is, a normal part of ageing.

prescriber.en: Prescribe growth hormone only for a confirmed deficiency or another approved indication, usually with an endocrinologist. For a request framed as anti-ageing, document the conversation, the evidence you quoted and the legal position, and decline.

clinical-staff.en: If a patient mentions growth hormone or 'HGH' for skin or energy, record what they use, where it comes from and any swelling, joint pain or tingling, and bring it to the prescriber.

advisor.en: You can explain that growth hormone falls normally with age and that trials in healthy adults show more side-effects than benefit. Anyone who wants to start it needs a prescriber's assessment rather than a product recommendation.

text.en: In the UK, somatropin is a prescription-only medicine licensed for growth hormone deficiency and specific growth disorders, and a Class C controlled drug.

In the EU, somatropin medicines have been authorised since the 1980s, through central and national procedures, for growth hormone replacement and for short stature in specific childhood conditions (EMA, 2012). The centrally authorised Omnitrope (since 12 April 2006) is prescription-only, and treatment is started and monitored by a doctor experienced in growth disorders.

In Portugal, somatropin medicines are authorised as restricted-prescription medicines, reserved for conditions diagnosed only in hospital or specialised settings, and INFARMED's register gives them no narcotic classification (25 September 2026). Growth hormone is distributed free of charge through hospitals with endocrinology or paediatric services, and a national commission (CNNHC) sets the conditions for its administration.

In Brazil, somatropin is registered for replacement therapy in adults with marked growth hormone deficiency, and it is a controlled substance on List C5 (anabolic substances) that needs a special-control prescription in two copies (RDC 1.036/2026). The Federal Council of Medicine's Resolution 1.999/2012, in force in September 2026, bars the use of hormones, including growth hormone, except in diagnosed deficiencies where replacement shows evidence of scientifically proven benefit.

In the UAE, the Emirates Drug Establishment (EDE) has held medicines registration since Federal Decree-Law 28/2023; the medicines law is Federal Decree-Law 38 of 2024, which prohibits advertising semi-controlled products to the public. Somatropin is registered with the EDE and is on the federal list of semi-controlled medical products (MOHAP Ministerial Decision 306/2023), and every somatropin entry in the EDE register is dispensed as a semi-controlled drug (25 September 2026).

prompt.en: Fictional chart note: a healthy 58-year-old asks for growth hormone 'for her skin' after an online test reported her IGF-1 as 'below the range for a 30-year-old'. She has no pituitary history. What does the evidence support?

text.en: Start growth hormone, because restoring a youthful IGF-1 thickens skin.

why.en: The much-cited skin result for that idea missed statistical significance, and trials in healthy adults show more side-effects than benefit.

text.en: Read her IGF-1 against an age-matched range; without a diagnosed deficiency, the trials show small gains and more side-effects, so growth hormone is not the answer.

why.en: Correct. A low-for-young IGF-1 is often normal for age, and the healthy-ageing trials point against treatment.

text.en: Offer a secretagogue instead, because it raises her own growth hormone more gently.

why.en: That is a mechanism argument. No secretagogue has trial evidence of benefit for skin or healthy ageing, as lesson 6.2 shows.

feedback.en: Treat a diagnosis, not a number read against the wrong age band.

body.en: Somatropin is growth hormone itself. GHRH analogues (sermorelin, tesamorelin, CJC-1295) stimulate the pituitary's GHRH receptor. Ghrelin-receptor agonists (ipamorelin, GHRP-2, GHRP-6 and the oral ibutamoren, MK-677) stimulate GH release through a second pituitary receptor. IGF-1 analogues such as IGF-1 LR3 bypass the pituitary altogether. They are sold as one family, and the next moments take them apart.

points.en: Replace: somatropin
Stimulate: GHRH analogues and ghrelin-receptor agonists
Bypass: IGF-1 analogues

blocks.sourceNote: Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology, ch. 3 · Peptide Pocket Guide, growth-hormone axis · Dominikowski 2026

body.en: Somatropin is recombinant human growth hormone. It replaces the hormone itself.
GHRH analogues and ghrelin-receptor agonists push the patient's own pituitary to release growth hormone, in pulses.
IGF-1 analogues act directly on the IGF-1 receptor, downstream of the pituitary.

audioScript.en: Four routes lead into the same axis, and patients rarely know which one they are on. Somatropin is growth hormone itself, made by recombinant technology. GHRH analogues, sermorelin, tesamorelin and CJC-1295, press on the pituitary's releasing-hormone receptor, so the gland releases its own growth hormone in pulses. Ghrelin-receptor agonists, ipamorelin, GHRP-2, GHRP-6 and the oral compound ibutamoren, press on a second pituitary receptor. IGF-1 analogues such as IGF-1 LR3 skip the pituitary and act on the IGF-1 receptor directly. Every route ends at that same receptor, which is why lesson three treats their risks together. Clinics often sell all of these as one family with one promise. Keep them apart, because the trials, the approvals and the side-effects belong to each molecule separately.

title.en: What real peptide evidence looks like.

body.en: Tesamorelin is the instructive exception on this axis. Both Hormonaly guides grade it A, for one indication. Read the record in order.

blocks.sourceNote: Falutz 2007, 2010 · EGRIFTA WR prescribing information (DailyMed, August 2026) · MHRA Products database (searched 25 Sep 2026)

note.en: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled and run by the developer, in adults with HIV and excess abdominal fat

value.en: About 15% less visceral fat than placebo at 26 weeks

note.en: Subcutaneous fat unchanged; the reduction held to 52 weeks on continued treatment
Reduction of excess abdominal fat in adults with HIV-associated lipodystrophy. The label says it is not for weight loss and that long-term cardiovascular safety has not been established.

value.en: IGF-1 above +2 SD in 47% at 26 weeks

note.en: Diabetes-range HbA1c in 5% against 1% on placebo; fluid retention; contraindicated in active malignancy

value.en: A, for HIV-associated abdominal fat only

note.en: No trial has tested skin, anti-ageing or general body shaping

callout.en: A GRADE A travels with its indication. The molecule does not carry it anywhere else.

text.en: UK status (MHRA products database, 25 September 2026): no UK product information. A search for tesamorelin returned no summary of product characteristics, patient leaflet or assessment report.

In the EU, tesamorelin has no marketing authorisation: the application for Egrifta (excess abdominal fat in HIV lipodystrophy) was withdrawn on 21 June 2012, when the provisional view of EMA's human-medicines committee (CHMP) was that it could not be approved, partly because raised IGF-1 was a major safety concern.
In Brazil, no registered medicine containing tesamorelin, including Egrifta, was found in ANVISA's register or online search (25 September 2026).

In the UAE, the Emirates Drug Establishment (EDE) has held medicines registration since Federal Decree-Law 28/2023; the medicines law is Federal Decree-Law 38 of 2024. No registered product containing tesamorelin, and none named Egrifta, was found in the EDE register (25 September 2026). In Dubai, the DHA prohibits prescribing, dispensing or using any peptide product that is not registered or licensed with the EDE (29 July 2026); in Abu Dhabi, physicians may prescribe peptide therapies only for clinical indications supported by available scientific evidence, after a documented eligibility assessment and with informed consent that covers the product's regulatory approval status (DoH, 31 July 2026).

body.en: A PubMed search in September 2026 found no randomized trial with a skin outcome for tesamorelin, CJC-1295, ipamorelin or IGF-1 LR3. The nearest is a 1997 study of a GHRH(1-29) analogue related to sermorelin, in 19 older adults. Skin thickness measured by caliper rose after 16 weeks, compared with a placebo lead-in rather than a parallel control group.

blocks.sourceNote: PubMed search, 24 Sep 2026 · Khorram 1997 · Dominikowski 2026

label.en: randomized trials with a skin outcome for tesamorelin, CJC-1295, ipamorelin or IGF-1 LR3 (PubMed, September 2026)

detail.en: Closest: a 1997 single-blind study of a GHRH(1-29) analogue, 19 older adults, skin thickness by caliper

means.en: Every skin promise made for these peptides rests on mechanism and anecdote. The nearest data are one small study without a parallel control group (D).

doesNot.en: It does not show these peptides harm skin or do nothing for it. It shows the question has never been properly tested, and a clinic brochure cannot fill that gap.

body.en: Seven products on this axis and the use each one is offered for. Decide what actually stands behind each before you see its grade.

note.en: GHRH analogue
Recombinant GH

value.en: Youthful GH levels in healthy adults

note.en: GHRH(1-29)

value.en: A weeks-long GH boost for skin and recovery

note.en: Long-acting GHRH analogue

value.en: Pulsed GH for skin and sleep

note.en: GHRH analogue
Ghrelin-receptor agonist

callout.en: A higher IGF-1 is a laboratory result. Benefit to a patient needs a clinical trial.

prompt.en: One product at a time: approval-grade trials, hormone levels only, or no human studies?

label.en: Hormone levels rise; no benefit shown

why.en: GRADE A. Two phase 3 trials and FDA approval in 2010, for this indication and no other.
GRADE A for diagnosed deficiency, on decades of trials. For healthy ageing, the trials show more side-effects than benefit.

label.en: Sermorelin, for youthful GH in healthy adults

why.en: In this course, GRADE D for this use. Small studies show GH and IGF-1 rising; none shows a clinical or skin benefit. Its former US approval was for children with GH deficiency.

label.en: CJC-1295 with DAC, for skin and recovery

why.en: GRADE D for any clinical use. Two phase 1 trials in healthy adults showed GH and IGF-1 rising for days; neither measured a clinical outcome. The Hormonaly guides rate it C; the trials stop at hormone levels.

label.en: CJC-1295 without DAC, for skin and sleep

why.en: GRADE D. No peer-reviewed human study of this form exists; its promises are borrowed from sermorelin and from the DAC version.
GRADE D for anti-ageing and skin. Human studies show GH release; its only phase 2 trial, in postoperative ileus, showed no benefit over placebo.

label.en: IGF-1 LR3, for muscle and skin repair

why.en: GRADE D. No peer-reviewed human study; mechanism and user reports only.

done.en: Seven sorted. Two have approval-grade trials, each for its own indication. Three stop at hormone levels, and two have never been studied in people.

title.en: Where each one stands in the US.

body.en: Dated to FDA's 503A category list of 14 May 2026, its Category 2 page (current as of 22 April 2026), the October 2024 advisory-committee votes, the bulks list in 21 CFR 216.23 and Drugs@FDA as checked on 24 September 2026. Absence from every list does not make a substance permitted, and FDA stopped placing newly nominated substances into categories in January 2025.

note.en: Growth-hormone deficiency and specific growth disorders; HIV-associated abdominal fat. Knowingly distributing growth hormone for other uses, anti-ageing included, is a federal offence (21 U.S.C. 333(e)).

value.en: No approved product on the market

note.en: Approved as Geref in 1990 and 1997, discontinued in 2008, approvals withdrawn in 2009 at the maker's request; FDA found in 2013 that this was not for safety or effectiveness reasons. In no 503A category.
FDA cites a heart-failure signal that stopped a hip-fracture trial early. The advisory committee voted 13 to 1 against adding it to the bulks list (October 2024).

FDA lists both among Category 2 nominations that were withdrawn, citing serious adverse events; ipamorelin remains in 503B Category 2. The committee voted 0 to 12, with one abstention, against listing ipamorelin (October 2024).
Nominated without adequate support for FDA to evaluate; both in 503B Category 2.

callout.en: The 503A bulks list holds six substances, none on this axis. Check the live lists before any conversation about compounding.

text.en: In the EU, somatropin has been authorised since the 1980s for growth hormone replacement and short stature in specific childhood conditions, while tesamorelin has no marketing authorisation (its application was withdrawn on 21 June 2012). No centrally authorised medicine containing sermorelin, ipamorelin or CJC-1295 was found in the Union Register or EMA's data (25 September 2026), and ibutamoren (MK-677) is not an authorised medicine: its orphan designation for growth hormone deficiency (20 June 2017) is, as EMA states, not a marketing authorisation.

In Portugal, no medicine containing tesamorelin, sermorelin, ipamorelin, CJC-1295 or ibutamoren (MK-677) is listed in INFARMED's Infomed register, which includes authorised, lapsed and revoked products (25 September 2026). Compounded medicines may use only raw materials listed in the Portuguese or European pharmacopoeia, another European pharmacopoeia or compendial scientific documentation, and one containing any other raw material may not be prescribed (Decreto-Lei 95/2004).

In Brazil, no registered medicine containing tesamorelin or sermorelin was found in ANVISA's register (25 September 2026), and ANVISA stated on 2 July 2026 that CJC-1295 and ipamorelin products are not registered with ANVISA and that any substance must have passed efficacy and safety assessment before it can be compounded. Ibutamoren is not a registered medicine, and ANVISA refused the clinical-trial petitions for ibutamoren mesylate on 9 June 2026.

In the UAE, the Emirates Drug Establishment (EDE) has held medicines registration since Federal Decree-Law 28/2023; the medicines law is Federal Decree-Law 38 of 2024. Somatropin is registered and dispensed as a semi-controlled drug, while no registered product containing tesamorelin, sermorelin, ipamorelin, CJC-1295 or ibutamoren was found in the EDE register (25 September 2026). In Dubai, the DHA prohibits prescribing, dispensing or using any peptide product that is not registered or licensed with the EDE (29 July 2026); in Abu Dhabi, the DoH's compounding standard treats peptides as non-monographed, high-risk substances and lets novel substances of unknown risk be compounded only if monographed, part of an approved medicine or listed on the DoH Registry for Compounded Substances (August 2026).

title.en: Name the indication before the molecule.

body.en: When a patient asks about a growth-hormone peptide, three answers come first. Which molecule, exactly, including whether 'CJC' means with or without DAC. What stands behind it, whether approval-grade trials for one indication, hormone levels only, or nothing. And where it stands in the US today, read off the live FDA lists. Tesamorelin's GRADE A belongs to HIV-associated abdominal fat and transfers to nothing else.

points.en: Which molecule, exactly
What stands behind it
Where it stands with your regulator today

blocks.sourceNote: Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology, ch. 3 and 15 · FDA 503A categories · 21 CFR 216.23 · EGRIFTA WR label · MHRA Products database (searched 25 Sep 2026) · MHRA Guidance Note 14

body.en: CJC-1295 with and without DAC are two products. Only the DAC form has been given to people in a trial.
Tesamorelin has approval-grade trials for one indication; the rest stop at hormone levels or have no human studies.
In the US, as of September 2026, no growth-hormone secretagogue is on the 503A bulks list.

audioScript.en: Imagine the request as it usually arrives. A patient says their clinic offers a peptide that raises growth hormone naturally, for skin and sleep, and asks what you think. Three answers come before anything else. First, which molecule, exactly, because CJC-1295 with and without its albumin-binding tail are two different products, and only the version with the tail has been tested in people. Second, what stands behind it. Tesamorelin has approval-grade trials for visceral fat in people with HIV, and the rest stop at hormone levels or have never been studied in humans. Third, where it stands in the United States today, read off FDA's live lists. As of September 2026, none of the growth-hormone secretagogues sits on the 503A bulks list.

prescriber.en: Tesamorelin is the only GHRH analogue with a current FDA-approved indication, and it is not a skin treatment. Do not prescribe compounded secretagogues on the strength of a mechanism; document what the patient uses and assess or refer any sign of GH excess.

clinical-staff.en: Ask which product, from whom and for how long, and record the exact name on the vial. Report swelling, tingling, joint pain or new skin changes to the prescriber. Do not advise on amounts or timing.

advisor.en: Describe these products accurately: one approved use for tesamorelin, hormone-level data or nothing for the rest, and no US bulks-list standing for the secretagogues. Refer anyone injecting them to a prescriber.

text.en: In the UK, MHRA's products database holds no product information for tesamorelin, sermorelin or ipamorelin (searched 25 September 2026), so any of them would reach a patient only as an unlicensed medicine. An unlicensed special needs a clinical need that no licensed medicine meets.

In the EU, tesamorelin has no marketing authorisation (its application was withdrawn on 21 June 2012), and no centrally authorised medicine containing sermorelin or ipamorelin was found in the Union Register or EMA's data (25 September 2026). EU law lets each member state, under its own legislation, allow an unauthorised medicine for an individual patient on a bona fide unsolicited order from an authorised health professional, under that professional's direct personal responsibility (Directive 2001/83/EC, Article 5(1)).

In Portugal, no medicine containing tesamorelin, sermorelin or ipamorelin is listed in INFARMED's Infomed register, which includes authorised, lapsed and revoked products (25 September 2026). INFARMED may authorise exceptional use (AUE) of a medicine without a marketing authorisation, for example when it is clinically justified as indispensable and no authorised alternative exists (Estatuto do Medicamento).

In Brazil, no registered medicine containing tesamorelin or sermorelin was found in ANVISA's register (25 September 2026). ANVISA stated on 2 July 2026 that products presented as peptides called ipamorelin that promise aesthetic effects or health improvements are not registered with ANVISA, and that some injectable peptides are not regularised in any category and are therefore illegal for any health use, including aesthetic use.

In the UAE, the Emirates Drug Establishment (EDE) has held medicines registration since Federal Decree-Law 28/2023; the medicines law is Federal Decree-Law 38 of 2024. No registered product containing tesamorelin, sermorelin or ipamorelin was found in the EDE register (25 September 2026). In Dubai, the DHA prohibits prescribing, dispensing or using any peptide product that is not registered or licensed with the EDE and bans misleading or unproven anti-ageing claims for peptides (29 July 2026); in Abu Dhabi, physicians may prescribe peptide therapies only for clinical indications supported by available scientific evidence, after a documented eligibility assessment and with informed consent that covers the product's regulatory approval status (DoH, 31 July 2026).

prompt.en: Fictional chart note: a 47-year-old has been prescribed a compounded 'CJC-1295/ipamorelin' product by a wellness clinic for skin quality. She asks whether it is 'basically tesamorelin'. What is the most accurate answer?

text.en: Yes. Both work on the growth-hormone pathway, so tesamorelin's approval covers the class.

why.en: An approval and its GRADE A belong to tesamorelin, for HIV-associated abdominal fat. They do not transfer to other molecules or uses.

text.en: No. Tesamorelin has phase 3 trials and a US approval for HIV-associated abdominal fat; CJC-1295 and ipamorelin have hormone-level data at best and no skin trials; neither is on the US 503A bulks list.

why.en: Correct. Different molecules, different evidence, different regulatory standing.

text.en: Yes, provided the compounding pharmacy is licensed.

why.en: A licensed pharmacy changes neither the evidence nor the fact that, in the US, these substances have no bulks-list standing.

feedback.en: Name the molecule, then its indication, then its status.

title.en: What too much growth hormone looks like.

body.en: Sustained GH excess changes skin in ways you can see. In acromegaly, glycosaminoglycan deposits and oedema make the face, hands and feet puffy and thick; the skin turns oily with large pores; sweating increases; skin tags and acanthosis nigricans appear. Drugs on this axis bring their own signs: fluid retention with swelling, joint pain, tingling and carpal tunnel symptoms. The Endocrine Society recommends measuring IGF-1 when typical acral and facial features are present.

points.en: Soft tissue: puffy, thickened face, hands and feet
Skin: oily, sweaty, skin tags, acanthosis nigricans
On treatment: swelling, joint pain, tingling

blocks.sourceNote: Ben-Shlomo & Melmed 2006 · Endocrine Society guideline 2014 · Acromegaly consensus 2024 · somatropin label

body.en: Glycosaminoglycan deposits and oedema thicken the skin of the face, hands and feet. Skin turns oily, pores enlarge, sweating increases, and skin tags and acanthosis nigricans appear.
Hands and feet enlarge slowly and the jaw widens. On GH-axis drugs, fluid retention brings swelling, joint pain and night-time tingling.

The Endocrine Society recommends IGF-1 for typical acral and facial features, and suggests it when several associated conditions cluster, including sleep apnoea, type 2 diabetes, carpal tunnel syndrome, hyperhidrosis and hypertension.

audioScript.en: Excess growth hormone leaves visible marks on skin and soft tissue, and noticing them early matters. In acromegaly, glycosaminoglycan deposits and oedema thicken the face, hands and feet, so features look puffy and coarse. The skin turns oily with large pores, sweating increases, and skin tags and acanthosis nigricans appear. Hands and feet enlarge slowly, and the jaw widens. Drugs on this axis bring their own signs, usually transient, with swelling, joint pain, tingling fingers and carpal tunnel symptoms. On somatropin, the label asks for existing moles to be watched for growth or malignant change. The Endocrine Society recommends measuring IGF-1 when typical acral and facial features are present, and suggests it when several associated conditions cluster. For most of you the job is recognition and referral, and the diagnosis belongs to endocrinology.

units.tutorContext: Module 7 closes the course: evidence appraisal, US regulatory frameworks and prescriber compliance, kept in separate registers. GRADE: certainty (high, moderate, low, very low; the guides print A–D) for one outcome across a body of evidence, never for a molecule; RCTs start high, observational studies low; rate down for risk of bias, inconsistency, indirectness (study PICO differs from the question), imprecision (CI crosses the important difference) and publication bias (suspect it when evidence is small industry-funded studies); rate up for large effects. Course examples: GHK-Cu's one indexed RCT measured post-laser healing (indirect for photoageing); BPC-157 wound data are rodent (indirect); LL-37 34-person positive then 148-person negative phase IIb (inconsistent); oral collagen benefit only in low-quality and industry-funded trials (risk of bias, Myung 2025). Lundh 2017 Cochrane: industry-sponsored studies more often favourable efficacy results, RR 1.27 (1.17–1.37). Grade and legal status are separate checks; mechanism never raises a grade. US 503A (21 USC 353a): identified patient, prescription; exempt only from approval, adequate directions, cGMP; bulk substance must meet a USP/NF monograph, else be an approved-drug component, else be on the 503A bulks list; registered manufacturer and valid COA; no statutory purity figure. 21 CFR 216.23: six substances, none a peptide, unchanged since 2019 (eCFR current 22 Sep 2026); listing is no endorsement. Categories 1–3 = interim enforcement posture: Category 1 includes non-injectable GHK-Cu (14 May 2026); 503A Category 2 has six substances; BPC-157, TB-500, KPV, injectable GHK-Cu, LL-37, melanotan II are withdrawn nominations with safety concerns still posted. PCAC 23–24 Jul 2026 is advisory; FDA staff concluded criteria weigh against listing BPC-157; only rulemaking changes the list. 503B: registered outsourcing facility, cGMP, risk-based inspection, adverse-event reporting, may compound without patient-specific prescriptions; products unapproved. >40 alpha amino acids = protein = biological product since 23 Mar 2020 (85 FR 10057); tesamorelin and hyaluronidase became BLAs; biologics cannot use 503A/503B exemptions; retatrutide residue count upheld by a district court in 2025, appeal pending (June 2026 filings). COA = supplier's report on one lot: MS identity (observed vs expected mass), HPLC purity (impurities unnamed), endotoxin (limit calculated from dose and route, FDA 2026 guidance), microbial, water, counter-ion, metals, solvents; cannot prove the vial is that lot, storage, sterility or legality; red flags = no lot, no chromatogram, no impurities, no endotoxin on an injectable, over 12 months old. FDA's BPC-157 briefing: public COAs mostly purity only; the nominator's COA reported no endotoxin test, and the COAs supplied were for the acetate while the free base was nominated. Ashraf 2024: three online semaglutide vials 7.7–14.4% purity vs 99% labelled, endotoxin in all. RUO: 21 CFR 312.160 permits shipment for lab or in-vitro research, 'Not for use in humans'; intended use judged objectively (21 CFR 201.128); a COA cannot convert RUO into a pharmaceutical. Cosmetic vs drug by intended use ('regenerate cells' is a drug claim; 'cosmeceutical' has no legal meaning); supplements not approved before sale; off-label applies only to approved drugs; unapproved new drug in interstate commerce is a prohibited act (21 USC 331); FDA's 2020 warning letter named compounded BPC-157 and GHK-Cu. Chart: article and status in those words; pathway, facility and COA if compounded; consent (not approved, foreseeable risks, approved alternatives incl. nothing, what happens if harm; elements borrowed from 21 CFR 50.25); grade quoted; monitoring and stopping rule; dated status check. UK (checked 25 Sep 2026; moments m7-p21, m7-p22): no 503A/503B; unlicensed medicines reach patients as regulation 167 'specials' (unsolicited order; doctor, dentist, nurse or pharmacist independent prescriber or supplementary prescriber; one patient's special needs; no advertising; manufacturer's specials licence, GMP-inspected site, product otherwise unassessed) or pharmacy preparation against a prescription (Medicines Act 1968 s.10); MHRA GN14 order: UK-licensed (even off-label) → licensed abroad → UK special → non-medicines such as supplements; special need excludes cost and convenience; prescriber responsible (GMC 102–108, MHRA DSU 2009, GPhC 2025, NMC Code 18). MHRA classifies by claims (websites, social media), form (injection) and use (GN8); no sale, supply or advertising without a UK marketing authorisation (HMR regs 46, 279); injectable melanotan = medicine (FOI 24/274); May 2026 seizure included peptide products; no POM advertising to the public (reg 284, CAP 12.12; Blue Guide: clinics may promote 'treatment for lines and wrinkles' without naming the POM; ASA 11 Feb 2026 Voy ruling on '#mounjaro' posts); GMC: physical examination before prescribing injectable cosmetic medicines. Never give doses, reconstitution, stacking, administration or sourcing; never validate a vendor or call a COA 'safe'. Adapt 'what you do next' to prescriber, clinical staff or advisor without changing grades or facts. The course is designed toward future CME accreditation; no credit is offered at this time.

videoTranscript.en: This last module turns the course into three habits. You will rate the certainty behind a claim with GRADE, read a compounding status and a certificate of analysis for what they do and do not prove, and write the consent and chart note that an unapproved product needs. Every claim you hear about a skin peptide carries a hidden question. How sure can we be? GRADE answers it with four levels of certainty, from high to very low. The rating belongs to a body of evidence for one outcome, such as wrinkle depth at twelve weeks, and never to a single study or to the molecule itself. Randomized trials start high and observational studies start low. From there, certainty drops for five reasons you can name, which are risk of bias, inconsistency between trials, indirectness, imprecision, and suspected publication bias. Both Hormonaly guides print a letter from A to D beside each use. Read those letters as the same four levels, adapted. They rate the evidence for that use, and they say nothing about whether a product is legal.

title.en: GRADE rates certainty in an effect, one outcome at a time.

body.en: GRADE sorts the evidence on a specific question into four levels of certainty: high, moderate, low and very low. The rating applies to a body of evidence for one outcome, never to a single study or to a molecule. Randomized trials start high and observational studies start low; certainty then falls for risk of bias, inconsistency, indirectness, imprecision or suspected publication bias, and occasionally rises for a very large effect. Both Hormonaly guides print the letters A to D for the same idea, adapted, and attach each letter to a specific use.

body.en: High, moderate, low, very low: how confident you can be that an estimated effect is close to the truth, for one outcome, across all the studies that address it.
Randomized trials start at high certainty and observational studies at low. The starting point then moves, for reasons you can name.
A to D in both Hormonaly guides maps onto the same four levels. The letter rates the evidence for a listed use. It does not rate legality, popularity or mechanism.

body.en: A Cochrane methodology review brought together 75 papers, each comparing studies sponsored by the manufacturer with studies funded in other ways. Industry-sponsored drug and device studies more often reported favourable efficacy results and favourable conclusions, and the difference was not explained by the usual risk-of-bias checks. It is the pattern you met with oral collagen in module 04.

label.en: risk ratio for a favourable efficacy result, industry-sponsored versus other studies

detail.en: Lundh et al., Cochrane 2017 · 95% CI 1.17–1.37 · moderate-certainty evidence

means.en: When a manufacturer pays for the trial, a favourable result is more likely. Funding is a reason to read a trial harder and to look for independent replication.

doesNot.en: It does not make a sponsored trial wrong or an independent one right. It describes an average tilt across many studies and says nothing about any single product.

body.en: GRADE names the ways a body of evidence can mislead. Read the four you will use most. Then sort four cases from this course by the reason that most lowers certainty. The fifth, publication bias, is suspected when the evidence is a handful of small, mostly commercially funded studies.

note.en: Flaws in design or conduct that can exaggerate an effect; check whether low- and high-quality trials disagree
Unexplained differences in results between studies of the same question
The studies differ from your question in population, intervention, comparison or outcome

prompt.en: One case at a time: which reason most lowers certainty here?

label.en: Topical GHK-Cu: the only indexed trial measured healing after laser resurfacing. Your patient asks about photoageing.

why.en: Indirectness. The trial's outcome, healing after resurfacing, is a neighbour of your patient's question, photoageing, so it answers a different question.

label.en: LL-37 in venous leg ulcers: a 34-person trial was positive; a 148-person multicentre trial was negative in its full cohort.

why.en: Inconsistency. Two randomized trials of the same question point in different directions, and the larger one found no effect overall.

label.en: Oral collagen: the pooled benefit disappears when only high-quality trials are kept.

why.en: Risk of bias. When low- and high-quality trials disagree, GRADE gives the high-quality ones the weight, and here they show no effect.

label.en: BPC-157 for skin healing: the wound data come from animal models, mostly rodents.

why.en: Indirectness. The population is animals and your question is about people, as indirect as evidence gets.

done.en: Four placed. Two were indirectness: real studies that answer a different question from the one in front of you. Imprecision comes back in the question that closes this lesson.

Check what the product legally is as a separate step. A good grade never makes a product lawful, and an approval says nothing about the grade for an unapproved use.
A persuasive mechanism leaves the grade where it is. Both Hormonaly guides say so in almost the same words.

audioScript.en: Suppose a patient asks whether a peptide works. Start with the outcome they care about, say fewer lines around the eyes, and give the certainty for that outcome, along with who paid for the trials behind it. Then, as a separate step, check what the product legally is. The Hormonaly guides keep these two checks apart for a reason. An approved drug can carry a low grade for the particular use a patient has in mind, and a compound with stronger human data may still have no lawful route in the United States. A persuasive mechanism leaves the grade exactly where it is. Whatever your role, say the outcome and the grade in one breath, and treat the regulatory answer as a question of its own.

prescriber.en: Before you recommend or prescribe, write the outcome and its grade in the note, and record the product's regulatory status on a separate line. If no trial addresses the outcome the patient wants, say so and record it.

clinical-staff.en: When a patient quotes a result, note which outcome it was and where it came from, and pass questions about grades and status to the prescriber rather than rating the product yourself.

advisor.en: Describe what a product has been shown to do, for which outcome, and who funded the trials. Leave the question of whether it can lawfully be prescribed to a prescriber.

prompt.en: A fictional serum's brochure says 'GRADE A: three randomized trials'. All three were run by the maker, enrolled 20 to 30 people each, lasted four weeks and measured skin hydration. Your patient wants fewer wrinkles. What is the most defensible certainty for that outcome?

text.en: High, because three randomized trials agree.

why.en: Randomized trials start high, but these are small, sponsor-run and measured a different outcome, and each of those lowers certainty.

text.en: Low or very low: small sponsor-run trials that measured hydration, not wrinkles.

why.en: Correct. Indirectness (the wrong outcome), imprecision (few people) and suspected publication bias (small industry-funded studies) all rate it down.

text.en: It cannot be graded, because industry-funded trials are invalid.

why.en: Sponsored trials are still evidence. Funding is a reason to rate cautiously and to look for replication; it never deletes a trial.

title.en: Two compounding routes, one strict order.

body.en: In the US, section 503A lets a licensed pharmacist or physician compound for an identified patient on a prescription, exempt from new-drug approval, adequate directions for use and good manufacturing practice. The bulk substance must meet a USP or NF monograph; failing that, be a component of an approved drug; failing that, appear on FDA's 503A bulks list. It must also come from an FDA-registered establishment with a valid certificate of analysis. Section 503B outsourcing facilities register with FDA, work to good manufacturing practice under inspection, and may compound without patient-specific prescriptions.

points.en: 503A: patient-specific, three exemptions
Monograph, then approved component, then the bulks list
503B: registered, inspected, held to good manufacturing practice

blocks.sourceNote: 21 U.S.C. 353a and 353b · FDA 503A bulks page (updated 14 May 2026) · FDA, information for outsourcing facilities

body.en: A licensed pharmacist or physician compounds for an identified patient on a valid prescription. Meeting the conditions exempts the product from approval, adequate directions and good manufacturing practice, and from nothing else.

Monograph first. Only if none exists, a component of an approved drug. Only if neither applies, the 503A bulks list. A valid certificate of analysis and a registered manufacturer are conditions as well.
Outsourcing facilities register with FDA, meet good manufacturing practice, are inspected on a risk-based schedule and report adverse events. Their products remain unapproved.

audioScript.en: Two routes exist for compounding in the United States, and the difference between them shapes the rest of this lesson. Under section 503A, a licensed pharmacist or physician prepares a drug for an identified patient on a prescription. If the conditions are met, the product escapes three requirements, namely approval as a new drug, labelling with adequate directions, and good manufacturing practice. The conditions start with the substance itself, taken in strict order. A USP or National Formulary monograph comes first. Only when there is none can it be a component of an approved drug, and only when neither applies can it sit on FDA's 503A bulks list. The substance must also come from a registered manufacturer with a valid certificate of analysis. Section 503B outsourcing facilities work differently. They register with FDA, work to good manufacturing practice, face risk-based inspection, and can compound without a prescription for each patient. Their products remain unapproved.

text.en: In the EU, medicines prepared in a pharmacy on prescription for an individual patient (magistral formulas) or to a pharmacopoeia for the pharmacy's own patients (officinal formulas) are outside Directive 2001/83/EC (Article 3). Pharmacists who prepare medicines solely for retail supply in dispensing pharmacies are also exempt from manufacturing authorisation (Article 40(2)).

In Portugal, a magistral formula is prepared in a community or hospital pharmacy on a medical prescription naming the patient, under a pharmacist's responsibility (Decreto-Lei 95/2004). Compounded medicines may use only raw materials listed in the Portuguese or European pharmacopoeia, another European pharmacopoeia or compendial scientific documentation, and one containing any other raw material may not be prescribed.

In Brazil, a magistral preparation is made individually by a pharmacy against a prescription from an authorised professional (RDC 96/2008). ANVISA stated on 2 July 2026 that any substance must have passed efficacy and safety assessment before it can be compounded, and that compounding may take place only individually, on a medical prescription, in a pharmacy licensed by local health surveillance.

In the UAE, where the Emirates Drug Establishment (EDE) has regulated medical products since Federal Decree-Law 28/2023, products compounded in licensed compounding pharmacies are exempt from marketing approval under Federal Decree-Law 38 of 2024 (Art. 5(2)), although such a pharmacy may not copy an EDE-approved product unless no commercial product can deliver the expected benefit, nor formulate products for research, development or experimentation (Art. 95). In Abu Dhabi, the DoH's compounding standard (August 2026) treats peptides as high-risk substances and lets novel substances of unknown risk be compounded only if monographed, a component of an approved medicine or listed on the DoH Registry for Compounded Substances. In Dubai, the DHA prohibits prescribing, dispensing or using any peptide product that is not registered or licensed with the EDE (29 July 2026).

title.en: A short list, three categories and a withdrawn table.

body.en: Dated to FDA's records as checked in September 2026. The bulks list is law, changed only by rulemaking; the categories are FDA's interim enforcement posture while nominations are evaluated. Neither is an approval.

blocks.sourceNote: 21 CFR 216.23 (eCFR, 22 Sep 2026) · FDA 503A categories (14 May 2026) · FDA safety-risks table (22 Apr 2026) · PCAC, July 2026

note.en: Unchanged since 2019. Listing carries no FDA endorsement of safety or efficacy.
FDA does not intend to act against compounders who meet its conditions. GHK-Cu for non-injectable routes is here (list of 14 May 2026).
Six substances under 503A as of 14 May 2026, kisspeptin-10 among them.
BPC-157, TB-500, KPV, injectable GHK-Cu, LL-37 and melanotan II among them. FDA's safety concerns stay posted; withdrawal is not clearance.
FDA staff concluded the criteria weigh against listing BPC-157. Only rulemaking changes the list.

callout.en: Check the live list on the day you prescribe. GHK-Cu alone moved twice in April and May 2026.

text.en: In the EU, no centrally authorised medicine containing BPC-157, TB-500, KPV, GHK-Cu, LL-37 or melanotan was found in the Union Register or in EMA's data on authorised, refused and withdrawn medicines (searched 25 September 2026). Copper tripeptide-1 (GHK-Cu) is listed in the Commission's CosIng inventory as a cosmetic ingredient with a skin-conditioning function (read 25 September 2026).

In Portugal, no medicine containing BPC-157, TB-500, KPV, GHK-Cu, LL-37 or melanotan is listed in INFARMED's Infomed register, which includes authorised, lapsed and revoked products (searched 25 September 2026).

In Brazil, ANVISA stated on 2 July 2026 that BPC-157 and TB-500 are not authorised as food supplements, and that peptide products such as GHK-Cu, BPC-157, and TB-500 that promise aesthetic effects or improvement in health conditions are not registered with ANVISA. No registered medicine containing KPV, LL-37 or melanotan was found in ANVISA's register (25 September 2026).

In the UAE, no registered product containing BPC-157, TB-500, KPV, LL-37, GHK-Cu or melanotan was found in the register of the Emirates Drug Establishment (EDE), the federal regulator of medical products since Federal Decree-Law 28/2023 (searched 25 September 2026). In Dubai, the DHA prohibits any peptide product that is not registered or licensed with the EDE (29 July 2026). In Abu Dhabi, the DoH puts systemic, regenerative or weakly evidenced peptides under enhanced controls (31 July 2026) and requires facilities to prohibit the import, distribution, marketing or use of Melanotan II (2 July 2025).

body.en: Since 23 March 2020 FDA defines a protein as an alpha amino acid polymer of more than 40 amino acids, whether or not it is chemically synthesized, so anything above the line is a biological product. On that date tesamorelin, a 44-residue GHRH analogue, and the enzyme hyaluronidase moved to biologics licences, and FDA told compounders that transitioned biologics cannot use the 503A or 503B exemptions.

blocks.sourceNote: 85 FR 10057 (2020) · FDA notice to compounders, March 2020 · FDA deemed-BLA list · Eli Lilly v. Kennedy (S.D. Ind. 2025; 7th Cir. No. 26-1301)

label.en: amino acids: above this, FDA treats the molecule as a protein, and so as a biological product

detail.en: 85 FR 10057, effective 23 March 2020 · tesamorelin (44 residues) and hyaluronidase moved to biologics licences

means.en: Size decides the rulebook. Peptides of 40 or fewer alpha amino acids stay drugs, so the 503A questions apply; above 40 the product is a biologic, and the compounding exemptions are closed to it.

doesNot.en: It does not make a short peptide lawful to compound; BPC-157 (15 residues) and GHK (3) still need a 503A route. How residues are counted can be contested: a court upheld FDA's count of 39 for retatrutide in 2025, and the appeal was still open at the latest filings (June 2026).

text.en: In the EU, tesamorelin has no marketing authorisation: the application for Egrifta, for excess abdominal fat in HIV patients with lipodystrophy, was withdrawn on 21 June 2012, when the provisional view of EMA's human-medicines committee (CHMP) was that it could not be approved.
In Brazil, no registered medicine containing tesamorelin, including Egrifta, was found in ANVISA's register or online search (25 September 2026).

In the UAE, no registered product containing tesamorelin, and none named Egrifta, was found in the register of the Emirates Drug Establishment (EDE), the federal regulator of medical products since Federal Decree-Law 28/2023 (searched 25 September 2026).

title.en: Outside the US, 503A does not apply.

body.en: FDA's 503A bulks list and its categories are US law and policy and apply only in the US. In the other jurisdictions in this course, a medicine without a marketing authorisation reaches a patient as a pharmacy preparation or an unlicensed supply made on a prescription, and the prescriber answers for that choice.

blocks.sourceNote: 21 U.S.C. 353a · FDA 503A categories (14 May 2026) · UK: Human Medicines Regulations 2012, Medicines Act 1968, MHRA, GMC, GPhC, NMC · EU: Directive 2001/83/EC · Portugal: Decreto-Lei 95/2004, INFARMED · Brazil: RDC 96/2008, ANVISA · UAE: Federal Decree-Law 38/2024 · read 25 September 2026

note.en: Set under US federal law and FDA policy; no other jurisdiction in this course applies them.

value.en: A pharmacy preparation or an unlicensed supply

note.en: Made or supplied on a prescription, for a product with no marketing authorisation in that jurisdiction.
The prescriber answers for choosing a medicine without a marketing authorisation.

callout.en: A 503A category means nothing outside the US: name the route your own law provides, and check it on the day.

text.en: The UK handles unlicensed medicines by a different route. A medicine with no UK marketing authorisation may be supplied to meet one patient's special needs, made to a prescriber's specification by a manufacturer that holds a specials licence, and it may not be advertised. The route (regulation 167): One patient, one prescriber, an unsolicited order. Made to the specification of a doctor, dentist, nurse or pharmacist independent prescriber or supplementary prescriber, for a patient under their direct care. No advertisement may be published. Who makes it: A manufacturer with a specials licence. The site is inspected for good manufacturing practice; the product itself is otherwise unassessed for safety, quality and efficacy. A pharmacist may also prepare a medicine in a registered pharmacy against a prescription. Special need: The patient's clinical need. MHRA's examples include an intolerance or allergy to an ingredient, or an inability to swallow solid doses. Cost, convenience and operational needs do not count. MHRA's order of preference: Licensed, then off-label, then imported, then special. A UK-licensed medicine comes first, even used off-label; then one licensed in its country of origin; then a UK special. Least acceptable are products that are not medicines where they are made, such as supplements. Responsibility: The prescriber's. Be satisfied the evidence supports safety and efficacy, take responsibility for the prescription and the follow-up, record your reasons, and explain them to the patient when the use is not routine. GMC, MHRA and GPhC guidance say this; nurse prescribers work within the NMC Code. Cost and convenience never justify a special, and a licensed option that meets the need comes first. Dated to the Human Medicines Regulations 2012 and MHRA guidance as read on 25 September 2026.

In the EU, a member state may, under its own legislation, allow an unauthorised medicine for an individual patient on a bona fide unsolicited order from an authorised health professional, under that professional's direct personal responsibility (Directive 2001/83/EC, Article 5(1)). Medicines prepared in a pharmacy on prescription for an individual patient (magistral formulas) or to a pharmacopoeia for the pharmacy's own patients (officinal formulas) are outside the Directive and need no marketing authorisation under it (Article 3).

In Portugal, INFARMED does not authorise the import of medicines for personal use (Circular 148/CD, 29 July 2011), but it may authorise exceptional use (AUE) of a medicine without a marketing authorisation, for example when it is clinically justified as indispensable and no authorised alternative exists (Estatuto do Medicamento). A physician who prescribes a magistral formula must satisfy themselves of its safety and efficacy, including possible interactions (Decreto-Lei 95/2004).

In Brazil, unregistered medicines may be imported only exceptionally, for strictly personal use and on a medical prescription, and import by any route is suspended when ANVISA publishes a specific prohibition; ANVISA stated in September 2025 that using an unregistered imported medicine is entirely the responsibility of the patient and the prescribing physician. ANVISA also stated in November 2024 that compounded medicines should be used only when the registered industrial product is unavailable in the dose or dosage form the patient needs.

In the UAE, Federal Decree-Law 38 of 2024 exempts products compounded in licensed compounding pharmacies from marketing approval (Art. 5(2)) and lets a physician prescribe a product never submitted to the Emirates Drug Establishment (EDE, the federal regulator of medical products since Federal Decree-Law 28/2023) for marketing approval only when necessary, with no equivalent alternative available and with the patient's approval (Art. 42(1)). In Abu Dhabi, the DoH's compounding standard (August 2026) allows compounding only for a genuine, documented clinical need that no suitable licensed product meets, and where permitted it limits prescribing to eligible facilities and credentialed prescribers, office-stock ordering to hospitals and DoH-approved specialty clinics, and dispensing by compounding pharmacies to individual prescriptions. In Dubai, the DHA prohibits any peptide product that is not registered or licensed with the EDE (29 July 2026).

title.en: What a certificate can and cannot prove.

body.en: A certificate of analysis is the supplier's own report on a named lot. Mass spectrometry checks identity, and a careful certificate prints the expected mass beside the observed one. HPLC gives purity as a percentage, which says nothing about what the impurities are. Endotoxin, microbial, water, counter-ion, metal and solvent results complete it. A certificate cannot prove that the vial in your hand came from that lot, how it was stored since, or that it is sterile and suitable to inject.

points.en: Identity: mass spectrometry, observed against expected
Purity: an HPLC percentage, impurities unnamed
Suitability to inject needs sterility, endotoxin and the right lot

blocks.sourceNote: Peptide Pocket Guide, peptide fundamentals · FDA PCAC briefing, BPC-157 (July 2026) · FDA endotoxin guidance (2026) · Popławska 2019

body.en: Mass spectrometry confirms the molecule's mass. A serious certificate prints the expected mass beside the observed one. In one seized vial, high-resolution mass spectrometry found an undocumented analogue of a known peptide.
HPLC gives the main peak as a percentage. When FDA's reviewers looked at public BPC-157 certificates, most reported purity alone, with no impurity limits.

The acceptable endotoxin level is calculated from the product's dose and route, so a figure without that context proves little. The certificate a BPC-157 nominator sent FDA mentioned no endotoxin test.

audioScript.en: Picture the certificate a patient hands you, and read it line by line, asking what each line actually tests. Mass spectrometry checks identity, and a careful certificate shows the expected mass next to the one measured. HPLC reports purity as a percentage of the main peak, which tells you how much else is present and nothing about what that something else is. Endotoxin matters for anything injected, and FDA's guidance says the acceptable limit is calculated from the dose and the route, so a bare figure settles little. When FDA reviewed BPC-157 for its advisory committee, most public certificates listed purity alone, and the one a nominator supplied mentioned no endotoxin test. Then remember what paper cannot do. A certificate describes a lot. It cannot show that your vial came from that lot, how the vial was stored, or that it is sterile.

body.en: A fictional certificate for a vial of a research-use-only peptide, sold online with injection instructions. Read each line, then decide which would count as useful evidence if it matched the vial, and which are red flags.

blocks.sourceNote: Fictional certificate · Peptide Pocket Guide, reading a COA · FDA BPC-157 briefing (July 2026) · FDA endotoxin guidance · 21 CFR 312.160

note.en: Same number as on the vial label
No chromatogram attached
Expected and observed mass both printed; spectrum attached
No impurity limits or results
Product page describes injection
No retest shown

callout.en: A clean certificate is necessary and never sufficient. It cannot make a research-use-only vial sterile, lawful or the lot you think it is.

prompt.en: Tap what each line is worth.

label.en: Useful, if it matches the vial
Lot number printed, matching the vial label

why.en: A matching lot number links the paper to the product in hand. It is still the supplier's own claim.
A bare percentage cannot be checked, and it says nothing about which impurities make up the rest.

label.en: Identity: expected and observed mass printed, spectrum attached

why.en: That is how identity is shown. It confirms the molecule and tells you nothing about sterility.
FDA's reviewers flagged exactly this for BPC-157: purity reported, impurity profile missing, so immunogenic impurities cannot be ruled out.

label.en: Endotoxin: not tested, on a product sold for injection

why.en: Endotoxin is a critical attribute for anything injected, and its limit depends on dose and route. 'Not tested' on an injectable is a hard stop.
Peptides degrade in storage; the Peptide Pocket Guide treats a certificate more than 12 months older than the purchase as a warning sign.

done.en: Six read. Two lines help if they match the vial; four are red flags. Even a perfect certificate leaves sterility, storage and lawful status unanswered.
